II. Software (Chapters 8-14)

Call Recording (Mind Legal Compliance):

Purpose

: Record important call content for meeting minutes, interviews, customer commitments, or dispute documentation.

Legal Reminder

: In China, the prerequisite for using call recordings as evidence is obtaining the other party's consent, or using them to safeguard your own lawful rights and interests.

How to operate
  • : Android usually has a clear "Record" button on the call interface; iOS does not provide native call recording and requires third-party apps.Spam Call Blocking and Smart Identification:
  • Principle: The Phone app queries a massive number database over the network, displaying "Spam Call", "Fraud Call", or company name upon incoming calls.
  • One-Party Recording vs. Two-Party Consent: Legally, recordings obtained "without the other party's consent" are not automatically invalid. According to relevant judicial interpretations by the Supreme People's Court, as long as the recording method does not seriously infringe on others' legitimate rights, does not violate legal prohibitions, and does not contravene public order and good customs, it can still be submitted as evidence. However, some provincial courts apply stricter admissibility standards for "secret recordings" in civil trials; criminal cases typically require even stricter legality review.
  • Regional Differences: Courts in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangdong, and other regions are relatively lenient regarding one-party recordings as civil evidence. However, recordings involving trade secrets or personal privacy require special caution in any province, as they may be excluded for infringing on privacy rights.
  • How to enable: Android typically has a clear "Record" button on the call interface; iOS does not provide native call recording functionality, requiring third-party apps or Bluetooth earbuds with recording capability.

Red Lines for Using Recordings

  • Recordings must not be used for extortion, distribution, or public humiliation of others.
  • Content involving third-party privacy (such as accidentally recording others' conversations) must not be casually shared.
  • In important scenarios, it's recommended to verbally notify at the start of the call that "this call will be recorded" — this is both compliant and strengthens evidentiary value.
In-depth on Harassment Call Management:
  • Traditional SMS has not been eliminated; it remains a reliable channel for receiving verification codes, bank notifications, and official information.iMessage
  • : Messages sent between Apple devices over the internet, displayed as blue bubbles. It supports high-quality photos and videos, read receipts, and is completely free with end-to-end encryption.RCS
  • Mainstream Caller ID Platforms: Domestic number tagging is mainly provided by three data service providers — Tencent Mobile Manager, 360 Mobile Security, and Dianhuabang (Tapir). Carriers' (China Mobile/Unicom/Telecom) "caller name" display and "harassment blocking" features also frequently use this data. Phone manufacturers (Huawei, Xiaomi, OPPO, vivo) mostly partner with these service providers for their tagging databases.
  • What to Do If Wrongly Tagged: If your legitimate work number is incorrectly tagged as "delivery," "courier," or "harassment call," you can appeal through the following channels:
    • Dianhuabang: Visit the number appeal platform (haoma.tk.cn) and submit your identity documentation.
    • 360: Submit through the "Number Appeal" feature within the 360 Mobile Security app.
    • Tencent: Submit through the "Number Appeal" page in the "Tencent Mobile Manager" mini-program.
    • Three Major Carriers: China Mobile users can send the SMS "KTFSR" to 10086 to activate anti-harassment features; China Telecom users can follow the "Tianyi Anti-Harassment" official account; China Unicom users can set it up in the "Unicom Mobile Manager" app.
  • Advanced Anti-Harassment: Enable your carrier's "high-frequency call blocking" (such as China Mobile's high-frequency call restriction) to automatically block AI voice robocalls.
What VoLTE/VoNR Are and How to Enable Them:
  • VoLTE（Voice over LTE）: Voice call technology based on 4G networks. Calls no longer fall back to 2G/3G, allowing simultaneous internet use during calls. Audio quality is clearer than traditional calls, and connection is faster.
  • VoNR（Voice over NR）: Voice calling based on 5G, the next-generation evolution of VoLTE. Features lower latency, better audio quality, and support for HD video calls. Requires all three: a 5G phone, a 5G plan, and local 5G coverage.
  • : Settings > Personal Hotspot/Tethering, turn it on.: On iOS, enable VoLTE in Settings > Cellular > Cellular Data Options > Voice & Data. On Android, find the "VoLTE HD Call" toggle in Settings > Mobile Network > Mobile Data > Advanced. Carriers usually enable it by default — if you find your network disconnects during calls and you can't access the internet, VoLTE is likely not enabled.

Uses Bluetooth or dedicated radio frequencies to establish point-to-point connections over short distances (usually a few hundred meters to a few kilometers).

If your phone's internet speed suddenly drops or disconnects during calls, it's likely because VoLTE/VoNR is not enabled, causing a fallback to 2G/3G networks. Once enabled, you can "browse videos while on a call."

: The next-generation communication protocol driven by global carriers and Google. Its features are similar to iMessage or WeChat, but it is based on phone numbers.

3. WeChat/QQ: Managing National-Level Social Apps

  • WeChat and QQ have transcended being communication tools to become "super apps" that integrate social, payment, and information acquisition.Chat History Backup and Migration:
  • Log in to the PC or Mac version of WeChat on your computer.Click the menu in the lower-left corner > [Migration & Backup] > [Backup & Restore].
  • iMessage and RCS Interoperability: Starting from iOS 18, Apple began supporting the RCS standard, meaning iPhones and Android phones can exchange HD photos, read receipts, and typing indicators via RCS, ending the "green bubble" experience gap. However, this requires both parties' carriers to support RCS and sufficiently new phone system versions.
RCS Deployment Status in China:
  • China Mobile: Deployed RCS relatively early. Some provinces already support the "5G Messaging" service, enabling rich media messages and interactive cards. Requires phone terminal support and activation at a carrier store.
  • China Telecom: Provides services through "Telecom 5G Messaging." Some plans support it by default; existing users need to send a specific SMS command to activate.
  • China Unicom: Deployed 5G Messaging in major cities, but terminal coverage is uneven. Many Android models still require manually enabling "Enhanced Messaging" or "5G Messaging" in the SMS app.
  • Actual Experience: Domestic RCS rollout has been slower than expected, mainly due to WeChat's dominant ecosystem and inconsistent terminal adaptation. Daily communication still primarily relies on WeChat, with RCS mainly serving as an "official push" channel (such as bank notifications and government messages).

Verification Code Security Red Lines

  • Never Forward Verification Codes: Anyone who asks you to "read out a verification code" or "forward an SMS" could be a scammer, including those claiming to be "customer service," "couriers," or "police/ prosecutors." Verification codes = your wallet.
  • Guard Against Phishing SMS: Be wary of links in SMS messages about "ETC expiration," "health insurance card frozen," "lost package compensation," etc. Legitimate institutions will never ask for your bank card number or password via SMS links.
  • Number Identification: Official bank SMS typically comes from short numbers starting with 95 or 1069 + company signature. Any "bank notification" from a regular 11-digit mobile number is almost certainly a scam.
  • Two-Factor Backup: Do not casually change the phone number bound to important accounts. If you must change numbers, unbind all critical accounts first — otherwise, the new number owner could reset your passwords via SMS verification codes.

Select "Back up chat history to computer", then select the chats you want to back up on your phone.

Deep Storage Space Cleaning Methods:
  • Standard Entry Point: WeChat [Me] > [Settings] > [General] > [Storage Space], where you can clear cache and finely clean chat history by time and file type.
  • In-Chat Cleaning: Enter a chat > top-right "..." > [Chat History] > [Manage Storage], where you can individually clean images, videos, and files from a specific chat while keeping text messages.
  • Original Photo/Video Cleaning: HD original photos and videos received in group chats take up the most space. You can batch-delete them by checking "Original Images" in [Manage Storage].
  • Turn Off Auto-Download: [Settings] > [General] > [Photos, Videos, Files and Calls], turn off "Auto-Download" to prevent silently caching large amounts of group files on Wi-Fi.
  • Mini-Program Cache: In [Discover] > [Mini-Programs], long-press unused mini-programs to delete them and free up their local cache.
  • Compressed Chat History Backup: When backing up on WeChat for Desktop, check "Compress" to reduce several GB of chat history to 30%-50% of the original size.
Group Management Tips:
  • Group Announcement: Published by the group owner/admin via the top-right "..." > [Group Announcement] in the group chat. Sends a strong reminder to all members, suitable for important notices. Automatically pops up for new members when they join.
  • Group To-Do: The group owner can set a pinned message as a "Group To-Do," and all members will see a red indicator that disappears after clicking to complete. Suitable for event sign-ups and task collection.
  • Group Sign-Up Chain: Type "#sign-up chain" in the input box to start a sign-up chain, suitable for ordering food or collecting registrations. Results are automatically summarized at the top of the group chat, avoiding message spam.
  • Group Live Stream: Top-right "+" in the group chat > [Group Live Stream] to start a live stream viewable only by this group, suitable for company training, family gatherings, and product testing.
  • Fold This Group Chat: Swipe left on the group name in the chat list > [Fold] to move unimportant groups into "Folded Group Chats," receiving notifications only when you're @mentioned.
  • Only Owner/Admin Can @All: When a group has more than 500 members, regular members cannot @all, preventing unwanted disturbances.
Moments Privacy Fine-Grained Management:
  • Group Visibility: When posting, tap "Who Can See This," select "Visible to Some" or "Hidden from Some" to precisely target based on pre-set tag groups (e.g., "Colleagues," "Family," "Clients").
  • Viewable Range for Friends: [Me] > [Settings] > [Friend Permissions] > [Moments] > [Range of Moments Friends Can View], with options for "Last 3 Days / 1 Month / 6 Months / All." Setting it to "6 Months" is recommended to balance privacy and social interaction.
  • Block Specific Moments Posts: Long-press a Moments post > [Don't View Their Moments] or [Unfollow]. The other person won't be notified.
  • Moments Ad Management: [Me] > [Settings] > [About WeChat] > [Personal Information & Permissions] > [Personalized Ad Management], where you can turn off behavior-based personalized recommendations.
  • Strangers' 10 Posts: [Friend Permissions] > [Moments] > [Allow Strangers to View 10 Moments Posts]. Turn this off to prevent strangers from browsing your past posts.

IV. Video Call Comparison

Different video call tools have different strengths. Choosing the right tool for each scenario makes communication smoother.

  • WeChat Video: Nation-wide coverage, suitable for all ages. Great for daily family communication and quick chats. Supports up to 20-person video calls (requires the "Group Video" mini-program). The downside is noticeable quality degradation on poor networks.
  • FaceTime: Exclusive to the Apple ecosystem, with excellent quality and end-to-end encryption. Starting from iOS 15, you can invite Android/Web users via a "Link," but the host must be on an Apple device. Suitable for cross-device family communication.
  • Zoom: The top choice for international meetings, supporting up to 100 participants with 40-minute free sessions. Features screen sharing, virtual backgrounds, and breakout rooms, suitable for cross-border/remote collaboration.
  • Tencent Meeting: The top choice for domestic office use, deeply integrated with WeChat, join by scanning a QR code. Supports 300-person meetings (paid version), with cloud recording, real-time subtitles, and meeting minutes — suitable for corporate training and large conferences.
  • Usage Scenario Recommendations: Choose WeChat for 1-on-1 daily communication; FaceTime between Apple users; Zoom or Tencent Meeting for formal business meetings (Tencent for domestic, Zoom for cross-border).
Network Bandwidth Requirements and Data Usage Reference:
  • WeChat Video Call: Requires approximately 500Kbps-1Mbps bandwidth. Standard quality consumes about 3-5MB per minute, HD about 8-12MB.
  • FaceTime: Standard definition about 1Mbps, 720p about 2Mbps, 1080p requires 4Mbps+. Data usage approximately 5-15MB per minute.
  • Zoom / Tencent Meeting: 720p about 1.5-3Mbps, 1080p requires 3-5Mbps. Hourly data usage about 300-800MB, with the host consuming more in multi-person meetings.
  • Recommendation: For extended video calls, use Wi-Fi whenever possible. On mobile networks, proactively lower video quality (turn off "HD Video" in app settings) to save data.
Video Call Quality Optimization Tips:
  • Lighting: Face the light source with your back to the window (natural light is best). Avoid backlighting that makes your face appear dark.
  • Angle: Keep the phone camera slightly above eye level to avoid a double chin. Hold the phone with both hands for stability during landscape-mode calls.
  • Audio: Use earbuds to avoid echo and feedback. Don't use "speaker" mode in quiet environments.
  • : Turn on "Find My Phone" and set a reliable lock screen password.: Prefer Wi-Fi. On 4G/5G, stay near windows to avoid signal degradation. In multi-person meetings, turn off other video feeds and keep only the speaker's.
  • Background Blur: Both Tencent Meeting and Zoom support AI background blur to hide cluttered backgrounds. Note: wear solid-colored clothing to avoid "green screen" glitches when your clothes match the background color.

Tips

When the network lags, turn off video and keep audio only — this is more polite than hanging up. Before important meetings, use Tencent Meeting's built-in "Network Test" feature to check bandwidth in advance.

V. Email: Configuration and Usage on Your Phone

  • Start backup on your computer: Open WeChat for PC > lower-left corner menu > [Migration & Backup] > [Backup & Restore].Select backup to computer: Click "Back up chat history to computer".
  • Select the content to back up on your phone and wait for the backup to complete.Chapter 9: Mobile Office and Learning
Differences Between IMAP, POP3, and Exchange Protocols:
  • POP3: Downloads emails from the server and deletes them by default, keeping only local copies. Suitable for single-device offline reading. The downside is that you can't see historical emails when switching devices. No longer recommended.
  • IMAP: Emails are always stored on the server, with local copies as cache only. Multi-device (phone/computer/tablet) sync is consistent — read on one device means read on all. This is the currently recommended protocol.
  • Exchange (including ActiveSync): Microsoft's protocol that syncs calendar, contacts, and tasks in addition to email. The top choice for enterprise email. Supported by Outlook, NetEase Enterprise Email, and Tencent Enterprise Email.
  • Selection Recommendation: Use IMAP for personal email; prefer Exchange for company email, then IMAP. Avoid POP3 unless you have special archiving needs.
Enterprise Email Configuration Methods:
  1. iOS: [Settings] > [Mail] > [Accounts] > [Add Account] > select "Microsoft Exchange" or "Other."
  2. Android: In the built-in "Email" app or Outlook app, select "Add Account" and enter your full email address and password.
  3. Server settings (using Exchange as an example): The server address is typically "mail.yourcompany.com" or "outlook.office365.com," with the domain being your company abbreviation.
  4. If prompted "Unable to verify server," enter manually: Incoming server (IMAP) port 993 with SSL encryption; Outgoing server (SMTP) port 465 or 587 with TLS encryption.
  5. After logging in, it's recommended to enable "Push" in [Account Settings] for real-time email, and turn off "Mail Preview" to protect business confidentiality.

Tip

Enterprise email typically requires an administrator to enable "client authorization password" or "IMAP/SMTP authorization code" — you can't use the web login password directly. If login fails, go to the web email settings first to generate an authorization code and then enter it on your phone.

Three cloud drives, each with its own job, not interfering with each other.5. A Real Mobile Office Scenario
  • Let me share a real experience of my own. Once on a business trip out of town, the client suddenly needed to revise contract terms. My workflow was as follows:At the hotel, I received the client's revision comments via WeChat (text messages + a photo of handwritten annotations).

The client raised a second round of comments, so I used WPS's brush tool to directly circle the revision positions on the PDF, with voice annotations explaining the revision approach.

After confirming everything was correct, used WPS's "Electronic Signature" feature to sign online, and sent it to the other party to sign as well.

To be honest, three years ago I would never have believed a phone could do these things, but now it really can. Chapter 10: Mobile Payment and Life Services

  1. To be honest, my parents' generation was initially resistant to the idea of "paying with a phone". "If the money is in the phone, what if it gets stolen?" This concern is very normal, but the reality is: the cash in your pocket has a much higher chance of being lost than mobile payment being fraudulently charged. Mobile payment is not about storing money in your phone — it's just a key, a key that opens your bank account.

  3. Whether you use Alipay or WeChat, the first time you bind a card, you need to go through these steps:
  4. Open the app, find "Me" or "Wallet". Tap "Add Bank Card".

Chapter 10: Mobile Payment and Life Services

The bank will send a verification code SMS to your reserved mobile number. Enter it and set a 6-digit payment password.

This payment password, your bank card password, and your lock screen password should ideally be three different passwords — don't set them the same for convenience.

A little tip: if you're concerned about security, you can open a Tier II or Tier III electronic account in your bank app specifically for binding to mobile payment. Only keep your everyday spending money in this card, so even if something happens, the loss is limited.

  1. 2. The Payment Code Is "Whoever Sees It, Takes the Money"
  2. Many people are confused about the difference between a payment code and a collection code, and this distinction is very important.
  3. Payment Code
  4. : The barcode + QR code you show to the cashier to scan. This code is equivalent to your "electronic wallet" — whoever scans it can deduct money from your account. So

absolutely never screenshot it and send it to anyone

. This code automatically refreshes once per minute precisely to prevent fraudulent use.

Collection Code

  • : Others scan this code to transfer money to you. This code can be screenshotted, saved, and sent to others — it's safe.Remember this distinction, and you can avoid many fraud traps. Anyone who asks you to "screenshot your payment code and send it over" is 100% a scammer.3. These Security Settings — 5 Minutes to Set Up Can Save You a Lot of WorryFingerprint/Face Payment
  • : In Alipay and WeChat's payment settings, turn on biometric payment. This way, every payment requires your fingerprint or face scan, so even if your phone is lost, the person who finds it can't spend your money.Security Lock

  1. Chapter 11: Photography and Photo Management
  2. To be honest, most people's phone photos fall far short of the phone's actual potential. It's not that your skills are bad — it's that you haven't noticed many small settings and habits. This chapter skips the fluff and only covers things you can use right away.
  3. 1. Have You Made These Mistakes Too?
  4. Let's first talk about the most common problems — see how many you've hit:
  5. The lens is dirty

Chapter 11: Photography and Image Management

You never adjust exposure

: In default mode, tapping the screen focuses, but if you swipe up or down after tapping, you can adjust brightness. Many people's photos come out either too dark or too bright simply because they don't know this operation.

The flash is always on

  • : The effect of a phone's LED flash is really ugly — the light is harsh and cold, making people look like ghosts. Unless it's truly pitch black, turn it off. In low light, Night Mode works far better than the flash.Zooming by pinching with two fingers
  • : Pinch-to-zoom on the screen is digital zoom, which essentially crops and enlarges the image, noticeably reducing quality. If you want to shoot something far away, use the zoom buttons on the viewfinder (0.5x/1x/2x/3x) — these are optical zoom and don't lose quality.2. A Few Small Tips to Immediately Boost Your Hit Rate
  • These don't require any theoretical knowledge — use them once and you'll see the effect:Rule of Thirds + Grid Lines
  • : Turn on "Grid Lines" (also called reference lines) in camera settings. When shooting, place what you want to highlight at the intersections of the four lines, and the composition will immediately "click". This is the simplest and most effective rule in photography — no mysticism, it just matches the visual habits of the human eye.: Pinch-zooming on the screen is digital zoom — essentially cropping and enlarging the image, which noticeably reduces quality. To zoom in on distant subjects, use the zoom buttons in the viewfinder (0.5x/1x/2x/3x). The 0.5x (ultrawide) and 1x (main camera) are native optical lenses with no quality loss; 2x/3x are typically "lossless quality zoom" — achieved by cropping from high-resolution sensors, with near-optical quality but not a separate lens. Beyond 3x is usually hybrid or digital zoom, with noticeable quality degradation.

: When shooting landscapes or street scenes, notice whether there are natural lines in the frame — roads, railings, walls, a row of trees — and let these lines extend from the edge of the frame to the subject. Use this technique well, and passersby looking at your photos will think you've studied photography.

Don't always shoot standing up

  • : Most people always shoot at their own eye level, so their photos all have the same perspective. Try crouching down for a low angle, or finding a high spot to shoot downward — the same place can produce a completely different feel. When shooting kids and pets especially, you need to crouch down — only eye-level shots produce a natural feel.Light is the top priority
  • : Shooting portraits under the bright midday sun produces hard, ugly shadows on the face. The best light is during the "golden hours" of early morning and late evening — the sunlight is angled and warm-toned, making everything look good. Overcast-day light isn't flashy, but it's even and soft, making it actually easier to shoot portraits than under bright sun.Night Mode essentials
  • : After turning on Night Mode, the phone automatically takes multiple shots and composites them. The most critical thing at this point is — your hand absolutely cannot shake. Lean against a wall if you can, rest on a table if you can, or hold your breath if you must. Night Mode requires you to hold steady for 2 to 4 seconds — any shake and the image blurs.3. Portrait Mode and Pro Mode
  • Portrait Mode: It produces the effect of a blurred background with a sharp subject (shallow depth of field). Because phones have small lens sizes, their real bokeh capability is limited, so this relies on AI algorithms — simply put, the AI cuts you out and blurs the background. The best results come at a distance of 1-2 meters; too far or too close and the algorithm easily makes mistakes. Also, when shooting portraits, make sure the background doesn't have overly complex lines, or the AI cutout may "fail" around the hair edges.
  • Pro Mode: If you want full control over the image effect, try Pro Mode. A few key parameters to know: the lower the ISO, the cleaner the image quality, but the darker the image; the slower the shutter, the more light comes in, but hand shake causes blur; white balance controls color temperature — set poorly, photos will look blue or yellow. Most people don't need to use Pro Mode year-round, but understanding these parameters at least lets you know what the camera is doing.

4. Photo Editing: Don't Overdo It — Just Right Is Enough

  • Many people misunderstand photo editing, thinking that editing makes it "unreal". In fact, photos taken by a camera are already different from what the naked eye sees — appropriate adjustment is to restore the scene you saw at the time, not to fake it.Snapseed
  • : A free editing tool from Google, professional features with no ads. My daily editing flow is: first use "Tune Image" to adjust brightness and contrast → use "Details" to sharpen → use "White Balance" to correct color casts → finally "Crop" to the desired composition. Snapseed's "Selective" feature is very useful — you can adjust only a specific area of the image without affecting the whole thing.Xingtu / Meitu

: These two are suitable for editing portraits. But I think there's a principle: keep beauty filters under 30% — beyond that it looks fake, with skin like plastic. Natural is more beautiful than perfect.

Lightroom Mobile

  • : If you're particular about color, this is the most professional. It has advanced features like curve adjustment and HSL per-color adjustment. But for most people, it's overkill.Editing Workflow Suggestion
  • : My own habit is to shoot the original photo first, then edit slowly on a computer screen or iPad at home — the phone screen is too small and the color isn't quite accurate. If you must edit on the phone, remember to set the screen brightness to medium-high, and don't edit in power-saving mode.5. Too Many Photos? Organization Strategies
  • Thousands of photos piled up in the phone album, taking forever to find a specific one — everyone has had this experience. Here are a few practical organization methods:Make good use of search
  • : Now both iPhone and most Android phone albums support smart search. You can search for keywords like "cat", "seaside", "ID card", "flowers", and the system will use AI to identify image content and find them for you. You can also search by date and location, like "last May" or "Beijing". Not many people know about this feature, but it's really useful.Regularly clean up junk

: Screenshots, duplicate photos, blurry failed shots — these are the real culprits taking up space. The iOS album has an automatic "Duplicates" merge feature; on Android, you can search for the "screenshots" folder in the file manager and batch-delete unneeded screenshots. I spend five minutes a month cleaning up and free up several gigabytes.

Create albums — don't rely solely on default sorting

  • : The system sorting by time is fine, but for cross-time content like "child's growth photos", "travel photos", and "important documents", you should manually create albums to categorize them. Apple's "Shared Albums" can even let family members add photos together — one person creates it, and the whole family can view it.Backup is the bottom line
  • : Photos are the most irreplaceable data — files can be recreated, chat histories can be lost and that's that, but a child's photos or an elderly person's videos, once lost, are truly gone. You must enable cloud backup. iCloud Photos is the most worry-free; on Android, each brand has its own cloud service, or you can use Baidu Netdisk / Aliyun Drive for auto backup. The principle is: have at least one cloud backup — don't put all your eggs in one basket.6. Screenshots and Screen Recording
  • Screenshots: Press the power button + volume up button simultaneously — a universal method for all phones. Many Android phones also support three-finger swipe down screenshots and knuckle double-tap screenshots. Long screenshots (scrolling screenshots) are well-established on Android — after taking one shot, tap the "Scroll" button, and the phone automatically scrolls down and stitches together a long image, suitable for capturing chat histories and web pages.
  • Screen Recording: Add "Screen Recording" from the Control Center, tap once to start recording, tap again to stop. Before recording, long-press the record button to choose whether to record microphone sound — turn on the mic if you're making a tutorial with narration, turn it off if you're just recording operations. The recorded video is automatically saved to the album.

Practice: Complete a Full Shoot + Edit + Organize on Your Phone

  • Turn on "Grid Lines" in camera settings, find a spot with natural light, and take three photos (remember to wipe the lens and adjust exposure).Select the best one, and use Snapseed for basic adjustments (brightness, contrast, cropping).
  • Create a dedicated album for this photo, named "My Works".Check whether cloud backup is enabled, to ensure the photo has a copy in the cloud.

Chapter 11 Appendix: Professional Imaging Technology Knowledge

  1. To truly understand the mysteries of phone photography and video, you need to know some professional imaging technology. This knowledge not only helps you better use your phone's camera, but also makes you more discerning when choosing devices.
  2. 1. Resolution, Frame Rate, and Bitrate: The Three Elements of Video Quality
  3. Resolution:
  4. Resolution determines image clarity, expressed in pixel count.

720P (HD)

: 1280×720 pixels, entry-level clarity.

1080P (Full HD)

: 1920×1080 pixels, currently the most mainstream resolution.

2K (QHD)

V. RAW vs HEIF vs JPEG Comparison

What Is RAW Format:

RAW format is the "raw data" recorded by the camera sensor — pure, unprocessed original information without any compression. It's like raw ingredients that need post-processing "cooking" to become a finished product. Phones, due to storage and processing limitations, default to "pre-cooked" JPEG or HEIF. RAW must be explicitly enabled.

RAW vs HEIF vs JPEG Comparison:
  • JPEG: The oldest format, best compatibility (any device can open it). 8-bit color depth, lossy compression, smallest files (2-5MB per photo). Limited post-processing room — forcing detail out of shadows produces banding artifacts.
  • HEIF/HEIC: Apple's newer format, files are half the size of JPEG at the same quality (1-3MB per photo). Supports 10-bit color depth and transparency channel. Drawback: some older devices and Windows require plugins to open.
  • RAW: Uncompressed raw data, largest files (20-100MB per photo). Color depth typically 12-16 bit, maximum post-processing room. Drawback: requires professional software (Lightroom, Snapseed, etc.) to open and process — cannot be shared directly.
Why Professional Photographers Shoot RAW:
  • Lossless White Balance Adjustment in Post: If white balance is wrong in JPEG (e.g., yellow under tungsten lighting), correcting it in post degrades quality; RAW lets you reset color temperature with zero loss.
  • Greater Exposure Tolerance: In JPEG, shadows underexposed by 2 stops are basically dead black — brightening produces noise. RAW can recover usable detail from shadows underexposed by 3-4 stops. Same applies to overexposure.
  • Richer Shadow and Highlight Detail: RAW's dynamic range far exceeds JPEG — much more latitude for preserving highlights without blowing out and shadows without crushing.
  • Sharpening, Noise Reduction, and Lens Correction All Controllable in Post: In-camera processing is a "one-shot deal." RAW can be adjusted repeatedly, always starting from the original data.
How to Enable RAW on Phones:
  • iPhone ProRAW: Only iPhone 12 Pro and later Pro models. Go to "Settings → Camera → Formats" and enable "Apple ProRAW." A "RAW" button appears at the top of the camera interface — tap to enable. Files are about 25MB each — enable only when needed.
  • Android Motion Raw / Ultra RAW: Naming varies by brand. Xiaomi/OPPO/vivo flagships have RAW toggle in camera "Pro Mode" or "More"; Huawei enables RAW in "Pro Mode"; Samsung Galaxy S series has RAW option in "Pro" mode. Files are typically 20-50MB.
  • General Advice: No need to enable RAW for casual daily shooting — files are too large and waste space. Only enable for important scenes (landscape, portrait, post-processing needed).

VI. Computational Photography Principles

Modern phone photography is inseparable from "computational photography" — using algorithms, not just lenses and sensors, to generate photos. Understanding these core principles helps you understand what your phone does the moment you press the shutter.

Multi-Frame Fusion:

When you press the shutter once, the phone actually takes multiple photos. The algorithm aligns and fuses the frames to produce one high-quality image.

  • Night Mode: Takes multiple underexposed photos within 1-3 seconds, aligns and stacks them — noise cancels out, brightness accumulates. The result: clean images even in low light.
  • HDR (High Dynamic Range): Shoots underexposed, normal, and overexposed frames (or more), then composites them into one photo with detail in both highlights and shadows. Especially effective for backlit scenes.
  • Deep Fusion (Apple) / Photonic Engine: For medium-to-low light scenes, analyzes and fuses multiple frames pixel by pixel, focusing on improving texture and detail — sweaters, hair, and similar details become noticeably clearer.
Semantic Segmentation:

AI doesn't process the entire image uniformly — it first "understands" what's in the scene — sky, faces, grass, buildings, clothing — then applies different processing strategies to each region.

  • Sky: Selectively enhance blue, reduce brightness to prevent overexposure.
  • Faces: Identifies skin tone areas, selectively brightens and smooths skin, leaving facial features and hair untouched.
  • Grass/Leaves: Enhance green saturation, boost detail sharpening.
  • Background Blur: In Portrait mode, AI identifies the subject's outline, blurring the background while keeping the subject sharp.
Deep Learning Applications:
  • AI Scene Recognition: The camera automatically recognizes scenes like "food," "pets," "night," "document" and optimizes parameters accordingly. For example, food mode enhances warm tones and saturation to make food look more appetizing.
  • AI Portrait Bokeh: Phone lenses physically can't achieve DSLR-level shallow depth of field. Deep learning models predict subject edges, then blur the background. Latest algorithms correctly handle details like hair strands and glass edges.
  • AI Eraser/AI Outpainting: Select passersby or objects in the frame, and AI "fills in" the occluded areas based on context. This is generative AI applied to imaging.
Computational vs Optical Photography:
  • Computational Photography Advantages: Good image quality in a small form factor, usable shots in extreme scenes like low light and backlight, and ordinary users can take "good-looking" photos without photography knowledge.
  • Computational Photography Disadvantages: Images can be "over-processed" — excessive sharpening, color distortion, unnatural sky colors; multi-frame fusion creates ghosting when subjects move; detail is "computed" rather than truly recorded.
  • Optical Photography Advantages: Large sensor + wide-aperture lens truly captures light, natural image quality, large post-processing room; no artifacts from algorithmic "hallucination."
  • Trend: Modern flagship phones combine "optical + computational" — large sensors capture real data, algorithms optimize the result. The two aren't opposed.

VII. Lens Types and Focal Lengths

Modern flagship phones typically have three to four lenses, each corresponding to a different focal length. Understanding focal lengths helps you choose the right lens for each scenario.

Common Lenses and Equivalent Focal Lengths:
  • Ultrawide (13-24mm equivalent): Widest field of view, suitable for landscapes, architecture, and interior spaces. Captures expansive scenes, but edges have distortion (straight lines curve), and faces stretch in portraits. Good for "big scenes," not for "close-ups."
  • Main Camera (24-28mm equivalent): The most commonly used lens, best image quality, widest aperture. Balances field of view and quality — works for both people and scenery. The "1x" on most phones is the main camera.
  • Telephoto (70-200mm equivalent): For distant subjects and portrait close-ups. Telephoto compresses spatial perception (distant mountains and nearby people appear closer together), producing more natural facial proportions and background blur in portraits.
  • Periscope Telephoto (200mm+ equivalent): Uses a folded reflective optical path to achieve longer focal lengths within the phone's thickness. Captures clear detail at great distances — suitable for concerts, sports, wildlife. Only on flagship models.
Sensor Size vs Pixel Size Trade-off:

The sensor is the "foundation," determining how much light can be captured. The industry says "a bigger sensor crushes the competition" — at the same pixel count, a larger sensor means larger individual pixels, more light intake, and better image quality.

  • Large Sensor: More light intake, better night image quality, wider dynamic range. Disadvantages: phone must be thicker (camera bump), higher cost.
  • High Pixel Count, Small Sensor: In sufficient daylight, high pixel count produces sharper photos, convenient for post-cropping. But in low light, each pixel receives insufficient light, producing more noise.
  • Mainstream Flagship Choices: Main cameras are typically 1/1.3-inch to 1-inch (some models already use 1-inch sensors), around 50MP — the balance point between image quality and size.
Pixel Binning Technology:

To balance high pixel count in daylight and large pixels at night, manufacturers use "pixel binning" — merging multiple small pixels into one large pixel for output.

  • Quad Bayer (4-in-1): 50MP sensor outputs 12.5MP photos. Each output pixel is synthesized from 4 adjacent pixels, increasing light intake 4x for cleaner images.
  • Nonacell (9-in-1): Used for 100MP+ sensors, outputs approximately 11-12MP. Same principle, even greater light intake.
  • Practical effect: In default shooting mode, you get the binned low-pixel photo — good quality, small file. When you need maximum detail (e.g., documents, distant subjects), manually switch to "high-resolution mode" for full-resolution output.

VIII. Special Shooting Modes

Beyond everyday photography, your phone has several special modes that, when used correctly, can capture shots you normally can't get.

Panorama Mode:
  • Move the phone slowly and steadily in the direction of the arrow — don't go fast, or stitching misalignment will occur.
  • Keep the phone vertically stable and only pan horizontally. If it bobs up and down, the horizon will become wavy.
  • Use with caution when there are moving people or cars — stitching may produce "half bodies" or "ghosts."
  • Panorama can also be shot vertically — vertical shooting with horizontal stitching, suitable for tall buildings or waterfalls.
Slow Motion and Time-Lapse:
  • Slow Motion: Shot at 120fps or 240fps high frame rates, played back as slow motion. Great for capturing water droplets, sports moments, and pets jumping. Requires ample light — slow motion mode has shorter exposure time, resulting in poor low-light quality.
  • Time-Lapse: Takes photos at intervals and combines them into a fast-forward video. Great for traffic, cloud movement, sunsets, and flower blooming. Shooting can take minutes to hours — always use a tripod to secure the phone; handheld shots will be blurry.
  • Tip: For time-lapse cloud photography, set up the phone and shoot for 15-30 minutes. The result is about 10 seconds of stunning time-lapse footage.
Starry Sky / Astronomy Mode:
  • You need to get away from urban light pollution — find a rural area or mountain with no streetlight interference at all. You can't capture the Milky Way in the city.
  • A tripod is mandatory — handheld shots will be blurry. The phone must be held steady for several seconds to tens of seconds.
  • Weather should be clear and cloudless, with the moon not too large (a full moon will overwhelm starlight). Dark nights around the beginning or end of the lunar month are best.
  • iPhone's "Night Mode" automatically detects starry skies and extends exposure time (up to 30 seconds); Android flagships' "Star Mode" or "Astronomy Mode" works similarly. Be patient — don't move the phone after pressing the shutter.
Macro Mode:
  • Used for photographing flowers, insects, jewelry, text close-ups, and other small objects. Can focus as close as 1-2 centimeters.
  • Some phones have a dedicated macro lens (usually a 2MP or 5MP small-sensor lens) with average quality; flagship phones use the ultra-wide lens to double as macro, producing better quality.
  • When shooting up close, the lens is very near the subject and may block light — use a desk lamp or flashlight to supplement lighting if needed.
  • The focus distance is extremely close, creating a very shallow depth of field — moving the subject a few millimeters forward or back can cause focus loss. Keep your hands steady and ideally have the subject stay still.

Practical Tips for Still Photography

  • Daily shooting: HEIF/JPEG default is fine — small file size and adequate quality.
  • Important scenes (landscape, portrait, post-processing needed): Enable RAW to preserve maximum post-processing flexibility.
  • Choose the right lens: ultra-wide for landscapes, telephoto for portraits, main camera for everyday use.
  • Night scenes and starry skies: Always secure the phone and enable Night Mode or Astronomy Mode.
  • Phones with large sensors (e.g., 1-inch sensor models) have higher quality ceilings, but shooting technique remains the key.

Try It Yourself: Understand Your Camera's Capabilities

  1. Check if your phone supports RAW shooting (Settings → Camera → Format). Try enabling it and take a shot, then compare the JPEG and RAW file sizes of the same scene.
  2. Switch between the ultra-wide, main, and telephoto focal lengths and shoot the same distant scene to experience the differences in perspective and image quality.
  3. Find a scene suitable for Night Mode or Star Mode, secure your phone, and take a night photo.
  4. Try shooting a large scene in panorama mode — keep the phone moving steadily.

  • : No matter which app you use, be sure to set the background to a warm yellow tone (eye-care mode), increase the font size, and widen the line spacing. Never read with white background, black text, and small fonts in low light for too long — eye fatigue accumulates.5. Mobile Gaming: Play Well, Without Harming Your Phone
  • My attitude toward mobile gaming is: playing is fine, but don't let it control you in return. Use gaming tools wisely to play more comfortably without delaying your real business.Game Mode / Game Space
  • : Mainstream phones now all have this feature. When turned on, the phone automatically clears background apps, blocks notifications, and prevents accidental touches — if you're in the middle of a team battle and a phone call suddenly pops up, Game Mode can block it for you. Some phones also support Performance Mode / E-sports Mode, forcing the processor to run at full speed, but at the cost of faster heating and battery drain.How to adjust image quality and frame rate

: Don't just max everything out. First ensure frame rate (smoothness), then pursue image quality. 60 fps is much smoother than 30 fps, but 120 fps puts a lot of pressure on the phone — mid-range phones shouldn't force it. If you play competitive games (like Honor of Kings or PUBG Mobile), frame rate priority is far more important than image quality — smooth control feel is a hundred times more important than pretty grass textures.

What to do when your phone heats up while gaming

  • : This is normal, but prolonged high temperatures will damage battery life. A few cooling methods: remove the phone case for better heat dissipation; lower screen brightness to around 70% (brightness is a major heat source); don't charge and play games at the same time (compounded heating kills the battery fast). If the phone gets too hot to hold, exit the game immediately and let it rest for a while.Anti-addiction tools
  • : iOS "Screen Time" and Android "Digital Wellbeing" both let you set daily time limits for game apps. I set myself a maximum of one hour on weekdays and two hours on weekends. When the time is up, the app icon turns gray and can't be opened. This limit is genuinely useful, not just for show.Cloud Gaming
  • : If your phone isn't powerful enough but you want to play big titles, you can try cloud gaming platforms (like Tencent START Cloud Gaming or NetEase Cloud Gaming). The game runs on a remote server, and the image is streamed to your phone as video. It demands a lot from your network but almost nothing from your phone's performance. The downside is that latency is unavoidable — suitable for strategy and RPG games, not for FPS shooters.Get Hands-On: Build Your Mobile Entertainment System

In the digital age, passwords are the keys to your front door. But with too many keys that are too complex, what do you do? A password manager is your "universal key keeper".

  1. 1. Why Do You Need a Password Manager?
  2. Modern people have an average of dozens or even hundreds of online accounts. If you use the same password for every account, once one website is hacked, all accounts are at risk. If you use a different complex password for every account, you simply can't remember them all.
  3. A password manager solves this dilemma: you only need to remember one master password, and it remembers all your other passwords for you.

2. How Password Managers Work

Encrypted Storage

: All passwords are stored with high-strength encryption, and only you can decrypt them.

Master Password

: You set a master password to unlock the password vault. The master password itself is not stored on the server.

Auto-Fill

  1. : On website or app login pages, the password manager automatically fills in your account and password.Password Generation
  2. : Can generate random, complex passwords to improve security.3. Recommended Mainstream Password Managers
  3. System Built-in:iCloud Keychain
  4. : The first choice for Apple ecosystem users. Seamlessly integrated with Safari and apps, free, secure. The downside is that cross-platform use is inconvenient.Google Password Manager

III. Introduction to Encryption Principles

Understanding the encryption principles behind password managers helps you judge whether a service provider is trustworthy. Below are several core concepts explained in plain language.

1. AES-256 Encryption

AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) is a symmetric encryption algorithm certified by the U.S. National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), widely used by banks, military, and government. "256" refers to the 256-bit key length — it would theoretically take longer than the age of the universe to brute-force. Mainstream password managers (1Password, Bitwarden, KeePass, etc.) all use AES-256 to encrypt your password vault.

2. Zero-Knowledge Architecture

"Zero-knowledge" doesn't mean the service provider stores nothing — it means thatencryption and decryption are both done locally on your device, and the server only stores encrypted ciphertext. The specific process:

  1. You enter your master password in the client.
  2. The client derives an encryption key from the master password (this happens on your phone/computer).
  3. Only the encrypted ciphertext is uploaded to the server.
  4. On next login, the server sends back the ciphertext, and the client decrypts it again using your master password.

Key Point:The master password itself never leaves your device, and the server doesn't have it either. So even if the service provider is hacked, the attacker only gets a pile of unbreakable ciphertext — unless they can guess your master password.

Why does "zero-knowledge" mean the service provider can't see your passwords either?

Because the decryption key is derived from your master password, which exists only in your mind and is used only on your local device. The service provider's server has neither the master password nor the decryption key — only ciphertext. That's why legitimate providers like Bitwarden and 1Password explicitly state "we cannot see your passwords either" — it's not that they don't want to, it's that they technically can't.

3. Key Derivation Functions: PBKDF2 and Argon2

The master password can't be used directly as an encryption key — it needs to be processed by a "key derivation function." The purpose of this function is todeliberately slow down computation, making the cost of brute-force attacks prohibitively high.

  • PBKDF2: A well-established standard, widely used by iCloud Keychain, Bitwarden, LastPass, and others. Slows down cracking through repeated iteration (typically 100,000+ times) of hashing.
  • Argon2: The winner of the 2015 Password Hashing Competition, more modern than PBKDF2. In addition to "computational cost," it introduces "memory cost" — making it difficult for specialized hardware like GPUs/ASICs to accelerate cracking. Already supported by Bitwarden, KeePassXC, and others.

Higher iteration counts are more secure but also slower to unlock. Legitimate providers publicly disclose their derivation algorithm and iteration counts for security community auditing.

4. Case Study: The LastPass 2022 Data Breach

In August 2022, the veteran password manager LastPass announced that its development environment was breached; in November of the same year, it further disclosed that hackers had taken backups of users' password vaults (encrypted ciphertext). Key lessons from the incident:

  • Zero-Knowledge Architecture Held the Line: Since the password vault was encrypted, hackers got the ciphertext but couldn't decrypt it — provided the user's master password was strong enough.
  • Users with Weak Master Passwords Are Most at Risk: Hackers can brute-force weak master passwords offline, so users with weak or reused master passwords face real risk.
  • Metadata Was Also Leaked: Although password contents were encrypted, metadata like site URLs and notes may not have been, revealing which services the user used.

Lessons Learned from LastPass

First, your master password must be long and unique (16+ characters recommended, with upper/lower case, digits, and symbols); second, prioritize providers that support Argon2id with high iteration counts; third, always enable independent two-factor authentication for high-value accounts (bank, email) — don't rely solely on a password manager.

  • Set a Strong Master Password: The master password is the last line of defense — make sure to set a long, complex password and memorize it firmly.
  • Enable Two-Factor Authentication: Turn on 2FA for your password manager account to add a layer of protection.

V. Real Password Strength Assessment

Password managers generally display a "password strength" indicator bar (red/yellow/green), but this assessment often only considers length and character variety, which isn't comprehensive. To truly judge whether a password is secure, you need to consider "entropy" and "whether it has been leaked."

1. Entropy: The Scientific Measure of Password Strength

"Entropy" measures the uncertainty of a password, measured in bits. The higher the entropy, the more attempts are needed for brute-force cracking.

  • "123456": Extremely low entropy, cracked instantly.
  • "P@ssw0rd": Appears complex, but appears in all dictionary attack lists, so entropy is still low.
  • "correct horse battery staple": Four random words, approximately 44 bits of entropy, far harder to crack than "P@ssw0rd."
  • 16 random characters (including upper/lower case + digits + symbols): Approximately 100 bits of entropy, uncrackable by brute force with current computing power.

Conclusion:"Length + randomness" is more important than "complex symbols". This is why the random long passwords generated by password managers are truly secure.

2. HaveIBeenPwned: Check If Your Password Has Been Leaked

Maintained by security researcher Troy Hunt, haveibeenpwned.com it collects accounts and passwords leaked in major data breaches. You can:

  1. Enter your email to check if your account was exposed in a breach.
  2. Use the Pwned Passwords feature to check if a password is in the known leaked database (password managers and browsers have this built in).

If a password appears in the leaked database,no matter how complex it looks, you must change it immediately— because dictionary attacks prioritize these known passwords.

k-Anonymity Query Principle

Worried that entering your password on HaveIBeenPwned will cause another leak? No need to worry. Modern queries use the "k-anonymity" protocol: the browser only sends the first 5 characters of the password hash to the server, the server returns all hashes starting with those 5 characters, and the comparison is done locally. In other words, the server never sees your complete password hash. 1Password and Bitwarden's "leaked password detection" both work this way.

3. Built-in Monitoring Features in Password Managers
  • 1Password Watchtower: Real-time monitoring of weak passwords, reused passwords, leaked passwords, expired passwords, and sites not using 2FA, displayed with red/orange/yellow severity levels.
  • Bitwarden Vault Health: Free version shows weak and reused passwords; paid version can detect leaked passwords (based on HaveIBeenPwned).
  • iCloud Keychain "Security Recommendations": iOS Settings → Passwords → Security Recommendations, alerts you which passwords appear in known leaks and which are reused.
  • Google Password Manager "Password Checkup": Built into Chrome, can one-tap check for leaked, weak, and reused passwords.

Check Now: Are Your Passwords Safe?

  1. Go to haveibeenpwned.com, enter your commonly used email, and see which breach events it appeared in.
  2. iPhone users: Settings → Passwords → Security Recommendations, address each red warning one by one.
  3. Chrome users: Settings → Passwords → Check Passwords, follow prompts to change.
  4. 1Password/Bitwarden users: Open Watchtower/Health Reports, prioritize "leaked" and "reused" items.

VI. Passkey: The Future of Passwordless Login

In 2024-2026, password technology is undergoing a revolution —Passkeyis poised to completely replace traditional passwords. Jointly promoted by Apple, Google, and Microsoft, endorsed by the FIDO Alliance and the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C), this is the biggest change in login methods in decades.

1. What Is Passkey?

Passkey is based on the FIDO2 / WebAuthn standard, usingon-device key pairsto replace passwords. The principle can be simplified as:

  • Your phone generates a key pair:Public key(registered with the website) + Private key(permanently stored in your device's secure chip).
  • When logging in, the website sends a "challenge," your phone signs it with the private key, and the website verifies it with the public key.
  • Before signing, you need to confirm your identity via biometrics (Face ID / fingerprint) or device PIN.
  • Throughout this process,no password is transmitted over the networkTrivia: What is README
2. Passkey vs. Traditional Passwords
Dimension Traditional Password Passkey
Phishing Resistance Poor, phishing sites can steal passwords Naturally phishing-resistant, private key only signs for real domains
Server Breach Impact Password hashes may be cracked Server only stores public key, no impact from breach
Convenience Requires memorization/entry/management Face ID/fingerprint login in one second
Replay Attack May be intercepted and replayed by man-in-the-middle Each signature is one-time, cannot be replayed
3. Platform Support Status
  • Apple iCloud Keychain Passkey: Native support on iOS 16+ / macOS Ventura+, Passkeys sync across all devices signed in with the same Apple ID, no need to recreate on new devices.
  • Google Password Manager Passkey: Native support on Android + Chrome, Passkeys stored in Google Account, sync across Android devices; since 2023, Google personal accounts support Passkey login.
  • Microsoft: Windows 11 / Edge already supports Passkey; Microsoft Account, Outlook, Office and other services are gradually opening up Passkey login, manageable in Microsoft Authenticator.
  • 1Password / Bitwarden: Already supports Passkey creation, storage, and cross-platform sync, freeing you from being locked into a single ecosystem.

Cross-Device Sync Is the Key Breakthrough

The biggest pain point of early Passkey was being "bound to a single device" — you had to recreate it when switching phones. Starting in 2023, Apple, Google, and Microsoft implemented cloud sync for Passkeys: iCloud Keychain syncs across Apple devices, Google Password Manager syncs across Android devices. Third parties like 1Password have enabled cross-ecosystem sync. This means Passkey is now practical enough to replace passwords.

4. How to Create and Use Passkey on Your Phone

iOS (iPhone) Path:

  1. On the account security page of a Passkey-supporting website (such as Google, Microsoft, Amazon, eBay, PayPal), select "Add passkey."
  2. The system shows a Face ID / Touch ID verification window. Once verified, the Passkey is automatically generated and saved to iCloud Keychain.
  3. Next time you log in to this website, enter your username and select "Sign in with iPhone" — just a Face ID scan and you're in.
  4. Management: Settings → Passwords → find the corresponding website to see the Passkey entry.

Android Path:

  1. On the account security page of a Passkey-supporting website, select "Add passkey."
  2. Google Password Manager popup → select your Google account → screen lock verification (fingerprint/pattern/PIN).
  3. Passkey is automatically saved to Google Password Manager and synced across Android devices with the same account.
  4. Next time you log in, select "Use Passkey" — just unlock your screen and you're in.
  5. Management: Android Settings → Passwords, passkeys & autofill → Password Manager → google.com.
5. Cross-Device Passkey Login

If you're on a Windows PC logging into a website that only has a Passkey on your iPhone, you can authorize via QR code scan:

  1. On the website login page, select "Use Passkey."
  2. Select "Use another device."
  3. The PC displays a QR code — scan it with your iPhone.
  4. iPhone shows a Face ID verification, and upon confirmation, the website login is completed on the PC.

This process uses dual encrypted communication via Bluetooth + internet — the Passkey private key never leaves your iPhone.

Try It Now: Experience Passwordless Login

  1. Sign in to your Google Account → Security → Passkeys → Add a passkey, experience Face ID/fingerprint login.
  2. Sign in to your Microsoft account → Security → Advanced Security Options → Add a passkey.
  3. Try it on services that already support Passkey, such as Taobao, JD.com, eBay, and PayPal.
  4. Keep traditional passwords as backup, gradually migrate high-value accounts to Passkey.

Transition Period Recommendations

Passkey hasn't completely replaced passwords — many websites are still in a "Passkey + password" coexistence phase. Recommendation: prioritize enabling Passkey for high-value accounts, butdon't immediately delete traditional passwords, keep them as backup; continue using your password manager, since not all websites support Passkey. Treat Passkey as a "powerful supplement to password managers" rather than an "immediate replacement."

VII. Hardware Security Keys

If your security requirements exceed those of ordinary users — for example, if you hold significant cryptocurrency, are an executive/journalist/activist, or protect enterprise core accounts — hardware security keys are a more reliable choice than SMS verification codes.

1. What Is a Hardware Security Key?

A hardware key is a physical device (shaped like a USB drive) with an internal security chip that stores your private key, requiring physical contact or NFC to complete authentication. Representative products:

  • YubiKey(Yubico): The most mainstream, supports FIDO2/WebAuthn, U2F, OTP, PIV, OpenPGP, with USB-C / USB-A / NFC and other interfaces. Series 5 costs $50-70.
  • Google Titan: Made by Google, USB-C + NFC / Bluetooth, about $30-40.
  • OnlyKey: Open-source alternative, supports multiple protocols.
  • Domestic Alternatives: Such as Feitian ePasskey, more affordable.
2. Why Are Hardware Keys Safer Than SMS Verification Codes?
  • Phishing Resistance: Like Passkey, hardware keys only respond to the real domain, so phishing sites can't trick them into providing verification codes.
  • SIM-Swap Resistance: SMS verification codes can be intercepted via SIM-swap attacks, while hardware keys don't need a phone number.
  • Man-in-the-Middle Resistance: The FIDO2 protocol includes a challenge value in each signature, preventing replay.
  • Physical Isolation: The private key remains inside the hardware chip forever — even if malware compromises your computer, it can't read it.
3. Applicable Scenarios
  • Cryptocurrency exchange accounts, wallet recovery.
  • Enterprise SSO, remote work VPN, SSH server login.
  • Email, GitHub, social media and other "master accounts" — once compromised, all other accounts can be reset.
  • Journalists, lawyers, executives, and other high-sensitivity individuals.
4. How to Configure a Hardware Key as Two-Factor Authentication

Using a Google Account + YubiKey as an example:

  1. Purchase a YubiKey (recommended to buy two at once — one for daily use and one as backup, stored in different locations).
  2. Sign in to myaccount.google.com → Security → 2-Step Verification.
  3. Select "Add security key" → insert the YubiKey into the USB-C port or tap it against your phone's NFC sensor.
  4. Follow the prompt to touch the YubiKey's metal contact to complete registration.
  5. It's recommended to register a second backup key.
  6. In the "2-Step Verification" settings, set the hardware key as the preferred verification method, with SMS as backup.

Websites with mainstream support: Google, GitHub, Microsoft, Apple ID, Facebook, Twitter, Dropbox, GitLab, AWS, Coinbase, Binance, and more.

Dual-Key Strategy

The biggest risk of hardware keys is "loss." Recommendations: ① Register two different keys simultaneously; ② Carry one with you (on a keychain) and store one in a home safe or bank deposit box; ③ Some websites allow printing "backup recovery codes" for offline storage. This way, even if the primary key is lost, you won't be permanently locked out of your accounts.

Be Careful with Purchase Channels

Always purchase from official stores or authorized dealers — don't buy used or keys from unknown sources, as pre-configured hardware could theoretically have been implanted with a backdoor. YubiKey firmware cannot be updated after manufacturing, but Yubico continuously publishes security advisories — follow their official website.

VIII. Family/Team Password Sharing

In family scenarios, Netflix, home Wi-Fi, router admin, and smart lock passwords need to be shared among the whole family; in team scenarios, servers, databases, and social media accounts require multi-person collaboration.Sending passwords via WeChat or writing them in shared documents are high-risk practices— once chat history or document permissions are leaked, the passwords are leaked too.

1. 1Password's "Shared Vaults"

1Password is the benchmark product for family and team sharing. Its core mechanism ismultiple vaults(Background).

  • Personal Vault: Only you can see it, for private accounts like banks and email.
  • Shared Vault: Family or team members can all see it, for shared items like Netflix, home Wi-Fi, and shared credit cards.
  • Permission Tiers: The team version can set certain members to "view only" or "view but not edit."

Family or team members don't need to share a master password — each logs in with their own account and can see the shared vault content they're authorized for. Password changes sync in real-time to all members.

2. Bitwarden's "Organizations" Feature

Bitwarden's free version supports individual password sharing (via the "Send" feature for time-limited sharing of a single password); the paid version can create "Organizations" to share entries with family or team colleagues with fine-grained permissions. Bitwarden also offers a self-hosted option, suitable for enterprises with high data sovereignty requirements.

3. Family Scenarios: Secure Ways to Share Netflix, Wi-Fi, and Other Passwords
  • Netflix / Streaming Sites: Store login passwords in 1Password Families' "Shared Vault" — family members log in individually without sharing in a group chat.
  • Home Wi-Fi Password: iOS devices can share Wi-Fi passwords directly via AirDrop to visiting guests without reading it aloud; Android 12+ also has a "Nearby Share Wi-Fi" feature.
  • Smart Locks, Smart Appliances: Use the manufacturer app's "Family Members" feature to create individual accounts for each person, rather than sharing one admin account.
  • Home Router Admin: Store the admin password in a 1Password Shared Vault, and set up a separate SSID for guest Wi-Fi.

1Password Families Value for Money

1Password Families costs about $4.99/month, supporting up to 5 family members, each with an independent personal vault + 4 shared vaults. That's less than $1/person/month — currently the best family sharing experience. Bitwarden's family plan at $10/year supports 6 people, offering better value but with a slightly less polished interface.

4. Team Scenarios: Server/Database Password Sharing
  • 1Password Teams / Business: Can create multiple vaults by department and project team, with fine-grained permission control and auditable access logs.
  • Bitwarden Teams / Enterprise: Open-source solution, self-hostable, enterprise version supports SSO integration and directory sync.
  • Separation of Duties Principle: Admin passwords should not be held by only one person — designate 2-3 "emergency contacts" to ensure business continuity when key personnel leave or take vacation.
  • Offboarding Process: Immediately revoke departing employees' password manager access, and rotate all high-sensitivity passwords they had access to if necessary.
5. Emergency Access: In Case Something Happens to You

Imagine a scenario: you alone manage all the family's important accounts, but you're unexpectedly hospitalized or pass away, and your family can't log into the bank, email, or insurance accounts.The "Emergency Access" featureis designed exactly for this — authorize a trusted family member/friend to access your password vault when you can't respond.

Bitwarden Emergency Access Setup:

  1. Log in to Bitwarden Web Vault → Settings → Emergency Access.
  2. Add the trusted contact's email and invite them to accept.
  3. Set a "wait period" (7-14 days recommended): the time window from when they make a request to when you confirm.
  4. If you don't respond during the wait period (decline or take no action), the other person automatically gains access after it expires.
  5. You can manually reject requests or revoke emergency access permissions at any time.

1Password Emergency Access:

  1. 1Password doesn't call it "Emergency Access" directly, but it can be achieved through the "Family/Team Organization" feature — after adding family members to the family plan, place some entries in a "Shared Vault."
  2. For individual plan users, it's recommended to tell one highly trusted family member your master password, or write it in a sealed envelope stored in a safe.
  3. 1Password also provides a "Recovery Code" — be sure to print and save it when enabling two-factor authentication.

Set Up Now: Leave a "Spare Key" for Your Family

  1. Choose a trusted family member as your "emergency contact."
  2. Set up emergency access in your password manager (Bitwarden) or add them to a family shared vault (1Password).
  3. Write the master password + recovery code on paper, seal in an envelope, store in a home safe or inform a trusted family member.
  4. Review every six months to confirm the emergency contact is still appropriate.

IX. Password Manager Best Practices

  • : Most password managers have a "security audit" feature that helps you find weak and duplicate passwords.Don't Forget the Master Password
  • : The master password cannot be recovered — forgetting it means losing all passwords. It's recommended to write it down on paper and keep it in a safe place.Emergency Access
  • : Set up an emergency contact, so if you can't access your account, a trusted person can obtain your passwords.Important Reminder

So the master password must absolutely not be the same as other passwords, nor written in an easily found place. Also, it's recommended to choose a service provider with a good security track record.Try It Now: Start Using a Password Manager

Import existing passwords (if any) or start adding new passwords.

2. Charging Mysticism? Fast Charging, Wireless Charging, and the Golden Rule
  • Does fast charging damage the battery?

Golden maintenance rule

  • : Try to keep the battery level between 20%-80%. Don't keep it starving (0%) or stuffed (100%). 3. Complete Guide to Fast Charging Protocols: Why Won't Your Charger Charge Fast?
  • Wireless charging1. Basic Principles of Fast Charging
  • Charging power = voltage × current (P = U × I). To increase power, you either raise the voltage, raise the current, or both. Different protocols choose different technical approaches.Fast charging workflow:

iPhone "80% Charge Limit" Feature — Turning the Golden Rule into a System Setting

The iPhone 15/16 series (iOS 17+) has turned the "20%-80% rule" into a system feature. When enabled, the phone automatically stops charging at 80%, significantly slowing battery aging. Settings path:

Settings > Battery > Battery Health & Charging > Charging Optimization > 80% Limit

The three options mean: ①No Limit— charges to 100%; ②Optimized Battery Charging— learns your routine, only delays to 100% during the last portion of overnight charging; ③80% Limit— stops at 80% directly, best for battery longevity. For people who are always at home/office with charging available, the 80% Limit is strongly recommended; for frequent travelers who need a full charge on the go, Optimized Battery Charging is a good choice.

GaN Chargers — A Traveler's Best Companion

You may have noticed that fast chargers are getting smaller and smaller — the hero behind this isGaN (Gallium Nitride)this new semiconductor material. Compared to traditional silicon-based chargers, GaN chargers have several clear advantages:

  • Compact Size: At the same power output, GaN chargers can be 1/2 or even 1/3 the size of traditional silicon ones. A 65W GaN charger is smaller than Apple's old 5W charger.
  • High Efficiency, Low Heat: Gallium nitride's switching loss is far lower than silicon, with energy conversion efficiency reaching 95%+, so it doesn't get hot during charging.
  • Travel-Friendly: A single 65W or 100W multi-port GaN charger can simultaneously charge a phone, tablet, and laptop — much lighter than carrying three "bricks."
  • Buying Advice: Look for GaN chargers that support the PD protocol (65W+ can charge laptops). Well-known brands like Baseus, Anker, Nubia, and Xiaomi are all good choices. Make sure to check that the cable is compatible (high-power charging requires a Type-C cable with an E-Marker chip).

Handshake phase

: The phone and charger communicate through the data cable, exchanging their supported protocols and power information.

Negotiation phase

: Both parties determine a commonly supported maximum power level.

Charging phase

  1. : The charger outputs voltage and current according to the negotiated values, and the phone manages the power.Adjustment phase
  2. : As the battery level increases, the phone gradually reduces the charging power to protect the battery.2. Mainstream Fast Charging Protocols in Detail

4. These Are the Real Battery-Saving Tips

  • Screen (the power hog)
  • : Lower brightness, shorten auto-lock time. OLED screen phones can save a lot of power with dark mode.
  • Poor signal
  • : In elevators and basements, the phone will desperately search for signal, draining power quickly.

IV. New Battery Technology: Silicon-Carbon Anode Batteries

If you've been paying attention to 2024-2026 flagship phone launches, "silicon-carbon anode" has practically become synonymous with premium batteries. This is an important upgrade to lithium battery anode materials, and the principle isn't complicated:

  • Traditional Graphite Anode: Phone batteries have always used graphite as the anode — the technology is mature and stable, but energy density has approached the theoretical limit (approximately 372mAh/g).
  • Adding Silicon Material: Silicon's theoretical specific capacity is about 10 times that of graphite (approximately 4200mAh/g). By adding a small amount of silicon to graphite to create a "silicon-carbon composite anode," the overall energy density of the battery can be significantly improved.
  • Energy Density Improvement: At the same volume, silicon-carbon anode batteries can increase capacity by approximately15%-20%. This is the key reason 2024-2026 flagship phones can fit 5500-6000mAh batteries in 7-9mm bodies.

Which Models Use It?

  • Honor: The Magic series pioneered the commercial use of silicon-carbon anodes. The Magic6 Pro, Magic7 series, and Magic V3 foldable all use it.
  • [Protect Privacy]: The Xiaomi 14 Ultra and Xiaomi 15 series feature a new generation of silicon-carbon anode batteries.
  • vivo: The X100 Ultra and X200 Pro series use a high-density silicon-carbon anode solution.
  • Huawei/OPPO, etc.: 2025-2026 flagships are widely following suit, and silicon-carbon anodes are transitioning from "black tech" to standard equipment for premium phones.

Practical Impact on Users: The biggest benefit of silicon-carbon anodes is "larger battery capacity at the same size" — phones can be thinner without sacrificing battery life, or the body stays the same thickness but the battery goes from 4500mAh to 5500mAh. In other words, you no longer need to pay the price of "thick and heavy" for battery life. Note that silicon-carbon anode batteries still need optimization with fast-charging chips for low-temperature and full-charge management, which is one reason manufacturers recommend keeping charging at 80% long-term.
