I have a friend whose phone was stolen last year. His first thought wasn't "how much was the phone worth", but "can I get my photos back?" Unfortunately, he hadn't enabled cloud backup. A phone is just a physical object, but the data in your account—once truly lost, can never be recovered. In this chapter, we'll talk about how to put real insurance on your digital life.

  1. 1. How Much Does Your Phone Account Actually Manage?
  2. Many people think an account is just for downloading apps. In reality, a phone account is tied to much more than you imagine:
  3. Contacts

Chapter 16: Account Systems and Cloud Services

Photos and videos

: From your child's birth to graduation ceremony, from first date to wedding trip.

Notes

  • ContactsApp purchase history
  • Photos and videosFind My Phone
  • : After your phone is lost, this is the only tool that can help you locate, lock, and remotely wipe data.If you use an Apple phone, all of the above is tied to your Apple ID. If you use Android, it's tied to your Huawei/Xiaomi/OPPO/vivo account, plus your Google account. These accounts are the "household register" of your digital life—lose the register, and many things become unprovable.
  • 2. Three Must-Do Things, Right NowEnable two-factor authentication
  • : Whether you use Apple or Android, the first thing to do is go to account settings and turn on "Two-Factor Authentication" or "Two-Step Verification". This is like adding a deadbolt to your door—password alone isn't enough, your phone also needs to receive a verification code. Even if someone guesses your password online, without your phone, they can't get in.Bind a reliable recovery method

: Two-factor authentication is secure, but there's a risk—what if you lose your own phone? So the system will prompt you to set up a "recovery key" or "backup email/phone number". This is your only way to get your account back in an emergency. Best to write it on paper, don't store it on your phone.

Confirm "Find My Phone" is enabled

  1. : This feature can help you locate, lock, play sound, and even remotely wipe all data after your phone is lost. It's the last line of defense. Many people skip this step when buying a phone, and when they want to use it later, they find it wasn't enabled—and it's too late.3. iCloud: The "Air" for Apple Users
  2. If you use an iPhone, sooner or later you'll face a soul-searching question: what to do when iCloud storage is full?Apple gives you 5GB for free, and honestly, this 5GB isn't even enough for one backup. So most people eventually receive that annoying popup: "iCloud Storage Full". At this point, you have three options:
  3. Clean up: Go to Settings → Your Name → iCloud → Manage Storage to see who's taking up your space. Generally, photos and backups are the biggest. You can delete unnecessary old backups first.

Upgrade

: 50GB is 6 yuan per month, 200GB is 21 yuan per month. Personally, I think 50GB is enough for most people, mainly for backups and photo thumbnails.

Workaround

  • : If you don't want to pay, you can periodically export photos to your computer, then turn off iCloud photo sync. But then you lose the convenience of automatic photo backup.An important reminder: iCloud Photo Library is not a "cloud drive"—it's "sync". If you delete a photo on your phone, it will also be deleted from iCloud. If what you want is "backup to cloud then clear phone", then iCloud Photos is not what you need—you need iCloud Backup, or a third-party cloud drive.
  • 4. Don't Confuse Sync with BackupThese two words sound similar, but the consequences are completely different:
  • Syncis bidirectional: Delete on phone, delete on cloud; delete on cloud, delete on phone. iCloud Photos, Contacts, Notes are all sync. The benefit is consistency across multiple devices; the downside is "once deleted, it's really gone".

Backup

iCloud+: The Privacy Trio for Paid Users

As long as you upgrade to any paid iCloud tier (50GB/200GB/2TB, etc.), you automatically become aniCloud+user, unlocking three privacy protection features:

  • Private Relay: Apple's version of a "VPN." Safari browsing traffic is relayed through Apple servers before reaching the website, so no one (including Apple) can simultaneously see who you are and what you're accessing. Ideal for protecting privacy on public Wi-Fi. Settings path:Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Private RelayTrivia: What is README
  • Hide My Email: Generates one-time random email addresses when registering on websites/apps, with emails automatically forwarded to your real email. If you no longer want emails from a site, simply turn off that random address — your real email is never exposed. Settings path:Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Hide My EmailTrivia: What is README
  • Custom Email Domain: You can use your own domain (e.g., @yourname.com) to send and receive iCloud email, suitable for personal branding or family email management.

Note: Private Relay is not available in some countries/regions, and domestic users may need alternative solutions.

iCloud Advanced Data Protection (ADP) — True End-to-End Encryption

In late 2022, Apple launchediCloud Advanced Data Protection (ADP), extending end-to-end encryption (E2EE) from the original limited data like Health and Passwords tothe vast majority of iCloud data— including Photos, Notes, iCloud Backup, device information, and 23 categories in total.

  • What Is E2EE: Encryption keys exist only on your devices — even Apple's servers don't have them. Even if Apple is hacked or law enforcement requests data, Apple can't produce decryptable plaintext data.
  • :(Background).Settings > [Your Name] > iCloud > Advanced Data Protection, and follow the prompts to set up Recovery Contacts/Recovery Key (Must Do— if you lose the key, your data can't be recovered either).
  • Notes: ① After enabling, you must properly safeguard the Recovery Key, otherwise data cannot be recovered if you lose account access; ② Shared Albums, iCloud Shared Photo Library, and a few other features don't participate in E2EE; ③ Apple IDs in mainland China do not currently support ADP — you need to switch to an account in another region.

One-sentence recommendation: If you have important private data in your account and your account region supports it, strongly consider enabling ADP — this is the strongest cloud data protection available to ordinary users.

is one-way: The phone takes a "snapshot" of its current state and stores it in the cloud. After that, if you delete something on the phone, the copy in the cloud backup is still there. iCloud Backup, local computer backup—these are backups. The benefit is safer data; the downside is they take up space and can't update in real time.

5. The Account Matrix for Android Users

  • The situation on the Android side is more complicated than Apple, because your data may be scattered across several accounts:Brand account
  • (Huawei/Xiaomi/OPPO/vivo): Manages your cloud space, Find My Phone, app store, wallet. Each brand has its own cloud service, usually a basic-free + paid-expansion model.Google account

: If you use Gmail, Google Photos, Google Contacts, these are all in your Google account. Google gives 15GB for free, more generous than Apple, but it's also shared with Gmail and Drive.

WeChat/QQ

  • : They are independent of the phone system. Your chat history and WeChat favorites are neither in the brand account nor in the Google account—they only exist on WeChat's own servers.So when Android users do backups, they need to check separately: brand cloud backup, Google backup, WeChat chat history backup—all three are essential.
  • 6. Family Sharing: Let Your Family Benefit TooApple's "Family Sharing" lets you share app purchases, music, movies, iCloud space with your family, and even share location. You can add up to 6 people. Setup method: Settings → Your Name → Family Sharing. Huawei and Xiaomi also have similar features, findable in account settings as "Family Sharing" or "Family Cloud".
  • A very practical scenario: Set up Family Sharing on your parents' phones, so you can always see their location (provided they agree). If an elderly person wanders off or can't be reached by phone, you have a location.The Consequences of Account Theft Are More Serious Than You Think

If a hacker gets your account password, they can: remotely lock your phone and extort ransom, view your photos and contacts, make purchases with your payment methods. More troublingly, if your account is tied to too many things, recovering the account itself is a nightmare. So, two-factor authentication—go enable it now.

Open phone settings, go to the account page, confirm two-factor authentication is enabled.

Check whether "trusted phone numbers" and "recovery key" are set up; write the key on paper.

Go to iCloud or cloud space management, see what data is syncing, turn off what you don't need.

Confirm "Find My Phone" is enabled.

If you use Android, check whether brand cloud backup, Google backup, and WeChat backup are all covered.

  • : If your car supports it (most new cars in recent years do), use a data cable to plug your phone into the car's USB port, and the car screen will automatically switch to the CarPlay or Android Auto interface. Some new cars support wireless connection, even more convenient.What it can do

UWB (Ultra-Wideband) Technology — More Precise "Spatial Awareness" Than Bluetooth

In addition to Bluetooth, new phones also contain a UWB (Ultra-Wideband) chip. Its capability isprecise distance measurement and spatial positioning— it can calculate how far another device is and in which direction, with centimeter-level precision. Bluetooth can only tell you "it's nearby," while UWB can tell you "it's 1.2 meters to your front-left." Common applications:

  • AirTag / Precise Finding: When an iPhone finds an AirTag, it shows directional arrow navigation like "7 meters away, go left" — this relies on UWB. Regular Bluetooth can only tell you whether it's within range.
  • Digital Car Keys: iPhones and Android flagships with UWB can serve as car keys — automatically unlock when approaching the vehicle, lock when walking away, and distinguish between driver and passenger positions to prevent relay attacks.
  • Indoor Navigation: "Aisle-level" navigation in malls and airports via UWB beacons, much more accurate than GPS.
  • Supported Models: iPhone 11 and later all have UWB chips (U1/U2); on the Android side, some flagships from Xiaomi, Samsung, vivo, and OPPO are also equipped.

LE Audio and Auracast — The New Generation Bluetooth Audio Standard

The classic Bluetooth audio (A2DP) used for twenty years is being replaced byLE Audio(Low Energy Audio), the new generation audio standard from Bluetooth 5.2 onwards:

  • Lower Power Consumption, Better Sound Quality: Uses the all-new LC3 codec, with better sound quality than the old SBC standard and lower power consumption — earbud battery life is noticeably extended.
  • Dual-Path Audio: Left and right earbuds transmit independently — switching to single-ear mode won't cause disconnection.
  • Auracast Broadcast Audio: The signature feature of LE Audio. A single phone/TV can simultaneously broadcast audio tocountless pairs ofearbuds — airport waiting areas, museums, gyms, and classrooms can all use a single transmitter for multiple people to listen with their own earbuds.
  • Current status: Flagship earbuds and phones released in 2024-2026 generally support LE Audio, but older devices require hardware upgrades and can't be software-unlocked. When buying new earbuds, check for the LE Audio/Auracast label.

: Navigation (much better than built-in car navigation), phone calls (answer from steering wheel), music (music apps on your phone directly cast to the car), voice WeChat (Siri or Xiaoai helps read messages and reply).

Old cars can use it too

  • : If your car is older and doesn't support it, buy an external CarPlay screen for a few hundred yuan, stick it on the dashboard—the experience is about the same.7. Security and Privacy in Integration
  • The more devices connected, the larger the surface area for privacy leaks. A few points to note:Before screen casting in public, first check whether your phone notification bar has any private messages—don't let the whole family see what they shouldn't.
  • Before giving or selling a device to someone else, unbind it first—go to phone settings, find that device, and select "Remove" or "Unpair".For smart home cameras, buy branded, encrypted ones—don't buy no-name ones for a few dozen yuan. There's been too much news about cameras being hacked for live streaming.

Try It: Cast Your Phone Screen to TV and Set Up a Smart Scene

Make sure your phone and TV are on the same Wi-Fi.

  • Find "Screen Mirroring" or "AirPlay" on the TV and turn it on.
  • On your phone: iPhone taps "Screen Mirroring" from Control Center; Android swipes down to find "Wireless Projection".
  • Cast your favorite photo to the TV for your family to see.

If you have smart home devices, try creating a "Leave Home Mode" in the phone app: one-tap to turn off lights, turn off AC, and start the robot vacuum.

What hurt her most wasn't the phone itself, but the three years of unbacked-up photos—every record of her child from birth to learning to walk. After hearing her story, I felt terrible, because this was completely avoidable. In this chapter, we'll seriously put insurance on your data.

  5. Stored locally on the phone, truly gone if lost

Case 1: Battery Life Optimization in Practice

Chapter 18: Data Backup and Migration

Stored on app servers, available by re-logging in on a new phone

: WeChat friend list, Taobao orders, transaction records in banking apps. These are stored on the corresponding company's servers, not on your phone.

In a gray area, requiring special handling

  • : WeChat chat history (although WeChat servers store it, you can't download it from the server yourself), device credentials bound to mobile banking, keys in two-step verification apps (like Google Authenticator).So what you need to focus on protecting is the first and third categories.
  • 2. Full Phone Backup: Get Everything in One GoA full phone backup is like taking a complete "snapshot" of your phone—current system settings, home screen layout, app data, photos, contacts, all packaged up.
  • Option 1: Local Computer Backup (Most Reliable, Recommended for People with Computers)iPhone

: Connect your phone to the computer with a data cable, open iTunes (older Windows version) or Finder (Mac), and select "Back Up Now" on the device page. Note: check "Encrypt backup", otherwise passwords and health data won't be included.

Android

: Each brand has its own computer software, such as Huawei Phone Assistant, Xiaomi Assistant, Samsung Smart Switch. Connect to the computer and follow the instructions.

The benefit of computer backup is that you don't need to pay for cloud space, and the restore speed is much faster than cloud restore. The downside is that you need to remember to plug in and back up periodically—most people can't manage this.
  • 3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things SeparatelyiPhone
  • iOSAndroid
  • : Each brand's cloud has backup functionality. Huawei phones search "cloud backup" in Settings, Xiaomi goes to "Xiaomi Cloud Service", OPPO/vivo similarly. There's also a Google-built backup (Settings → System → Backup)—turn this on too.
The biggest benefit of cloud backup is "you don't have to worry about it"—it's automatic. The biggest downside is that restoring takes a long time to download, and the free space is usually not enough.
  • 3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things SeparatelyFull phone backup is the safety net, but some things are too important and deserve a separate extra copy:
  • iOSDual insurance plan
  • : Enable iCloud Photos/Google Photos auto-sync, and every few months manually copy photos to your computer or external hard drive. This way, one copy in the cloud, one copy locally—mutual backup.

Free plan

: Google Photos gives 15GB for free, can be set to "compressed quality" to save space. Or every month, use a data cable to copy all photos to your computer.

Contacts (Easily Overlooked but Extremely Important)
  • iPhone contacts sync with iCloud by default—as long as sync is on, no extra backup needed. But if you want to be safer, you can export a vCard file from iCloud.com and save it on your computer.Android contacts usually sync with Google or brand cloud. Go to the Contacts app settings to export a .vcf file—that's a complete backup.
  • WeChat Chat History (Handle Separately, Top Priority)This must be discussed separately, because WeChat chat history is often incomplete in full phone backups, and phone migration tools simply can't handle it.
Method 1: Migrate to new phone
  • . WeChat → Me → Settings → General → Chat History Migration & Backup → Migrate → Migrate to Phone/Tablet. Connect both old and new phones to the same Wi-Fi, scan the QR code to transfer. Note: Don't log out of WeChat on the old phone until migration is complete.
  • Method 2: Back up to computer
. Install WeChat PC version on your computer, three bars in the bottom left → Migration & Backup → Backup & Restore → Back up chat history to computer. Afterward, when you change phones, you can restore it to the new phone.

Method 3: Back up to cloud

  • . WeChat also supports backing up to iCloud or phone cloud space, but note: this backup can only be restored on your current phone, not cross-device. To change phones, you still need to use the first two methods.4. Phone Replacement Guide: From Old Phone to New Phone
  • Getting a new phone is a happy event, but if the data doesn't transfer over, it becomes a headache. Three scenarios, handled separately:Same Brand Upgrade (Simplest)
  • iPhone → New iPhone: When turning on and activating, place the old phone nearby, and "Quick Start" will automatically pop up. Use the old phone to scan the pattern on the new phone. All data, settings, and app layout will be transferred intact, including Wi-Fi passwords. Takes about 20-30 minutes.

Android same brand

: Use the brand's built-in phone replacement tool. Huawei uses "Phone Clone", Xiaomi uses "Xiaomi Phone Transfer", OPPO uses "Phone Move", vivo uses "EasyShare". The steps are similar: install the same app on both old and new phones, scan to connect, check what to transfer, start.

Cross-Brand Phone Replacement (Android to Android, Different Brands)
  • Use third-party phone replacement tools or the old brand's built-in replacement app (most brands' replacement apps also support transferring to other Android phones). What can be transferred: contacts, photos, text messages, call logs, some apps. What can't be transferred: in-app login status (you need to re-login), WeChat chat history (use WeChat's own migration feature).Cross-Platform Phone Replacement (Android to iPhone, or Vice Versa)
  • Android → iPhone: Apple has a "Move to iOS" app. Download it on your Android phone, and when activating the new iPhone, select "Move Data from Android". Can transfer contacts, photos, text messages and other basic data, but app data can't be transferred. WeChat chat history still needs WeChat's own migration feature.
iPhone → Android

: Each Android brand has corresponding migration tools, but honestly, cross-platform migration experience isn't as good as same-platform. Do the most important things first: export contacts, back up photos, migrate WeChat chat history. Take your time with the rest.

5. The Golden Rule of Backup: The 3-2-1 Principle
  • This is a classic principle in the data security field, simple and easy to remember:3
  • : Keep at least three copies of important data (one original, two backups).2

: Use two different storage media for backups (e.g., one in the cloud, one on an external hard drive).

1

  • : At least one backup should be in a different physical location (to prevent fire, theft, etc. from destroying all data at once).For ordinary people, achieving "one in the cloud, one on the computer" is already quite good. Don't make it too complicated—the key is that you actually do it.
  • Special Attention for WeChat Chat HistoryWeChat chat history cannot be migrated by any phone replacement tool! It's not covered by full phone backup. You must use WeChat's built-in "Chat History Migration" feature, or back up to the computer version of WeChat. Many people discover after getting a new phone that all chat history is gone—and by then it's too late. The old phone may have already been factory reset.
  • Practice: Do a Complete Backup DrillCheck whether iCloud Backup or brand cloud backup is enabled, confirm the last backup time.

Manually back up photos: Use a data cable to connect to the computer, copy the DCIM and Pictures folders to the computer.

Back up contacts: iPhone users export vCard from iCloud.com; Android users export .vcf file in Contacts app settings.

Back up WeChat chat history: Open WeChat → Me → Settings → General → Chat History Migration & Backup → Back up to computer.

Copy the exported contacts vcf and photo folders to an external hard drive or USB drive, completing the "one offline copy elsewhere" of the 3-2-1 rule.

  1. Chapter 19: Troubleshooting and Self-Rescue
  2. Phones, like people, occasionally "get sick". Lagging, crashing, black screen, won't charge... most of these issues aren't that scary, and you can try fixing them yourself before sending it for repair. This chapter is your "phone emergency manual"—try low-cost methods first, then seek a professional doctor if needed.
  3. 1. Phone Lagging and Overheating—The Most Frequently Asked Question
  4. Honestly, it's totally normal for a phone to start lagging after about a year of use. The reason isn't necessarily that the phone is broken—more often it's "dust accumulation"—junk files, background processes, storage space slowly filling up.
  5. Diagnose First, Don't Rush to Fix:

Check storage space

: Go to Settings → Storage to see remaining space. If it's under 10%, the system will become very laggy because it's struggling to free up space. My experience: keep at least 15%-20% free space for the phone to run smoothly.

Check power consumption ranking

: Go to battery settings to see the power consumption ranking over the past 24 hours. If an app takes a large share but you barely used it, it's running in the background. Uninstall it directly or restrict background activity.

Think about what you did recently
  1. : Did it start lagging after a system upgrade? (It's normal to lag for the first few days after a major version update, as the system rebuilds indexes in the background.) Or did it start lagging after installing a certain new app? (Try uninstalling it.)Look at the usage environment
  2. : If the phone is left in the blazing sun, or in a thick case while charging and playing games, overheating is inevitable. High temperature also causes the CPU to automatically throttle, making the phone feel suddenly laggy. Let it cool down and try again.Treatment methods (from simple to complex)
  3. : Restart the phone (solves 60% of problems) → Clean up storage space (delete useless apps and videos) → If a specific app is causing trouble, clear its cache or uninstall and reinstall → Last resort: Back up data and factory reset.2. App Crashes and Unresponsiveness—When Apps Misbehave
  4. An app crashes when you open it, or suddenly freezes while in use. The handling process is like a doctor's consultation—step by step:Close and reopen first

: Swipe away the app from the background, then reopen it. Most temporary bugs are fixed with this one move.Update the app

: Check the app store for updates. Sometimes it's because the app version is too old and incompatible with the system.

Check permissions

  1. : Some apps need a certain permission to work properly, but you didn't grant it. For example, a camera app crashes when opened because it doesn't have camera permission. Go to Settings, find that app, and grant the necessary permissions.Clear cache
  2. : Go to Settings → App Management → Find that app → Storage → Clear Cache. Note: "Clear Cache", not "Clear Data"! Clearing data will delete all your login status and settings in the app, equivalent to factory resetting the app.Uninstall and reinstall
  3. : The last resort. Before uninstalling, confirm whether the app's data will be lost—for WeChat, back up chat history first; for games, confirm whether your account is bound to a phone number.3. Won't Charge or Charges Slowly—It Might Not Be the Battery's Fault
  4. Not being able to charge is a particularly anxiety-inducing problem, but often the cause is with the accessories, not the phone being broken.Check the charging port first
  5. : Use a toothpick or non-conductive small tool to gently clean out dust and lint from the charging port. I've encountered this myself—a thread from my pocket happened to block the charging port. When I plugged it in, I thought it was poor contact, but after cleaning it out, it was fine.Try a different cable and charger

: Cables have a much higher failure rate than chargers, especially cables that are often rolled up. Swap in a known-good cable and charger for cross-testing to quickly determine which accessory is broken.

Wireless charging issues

  • : If you use wireless charging, check whether the phone case is too thick, or whether there's a metal plate on the back of the case (like a magnetic mount). Also, place the phone precisely in the center of the charging pad—if it's off, it may not charge.Slow charging
  • : Confirm the charger's power is sufficient (iPhone needs at least a 20W PD charger for fast charging), the cable supports fast charging (not all cables can handle 3A+ current), and the phone isn't too hot (too hot will automatically reduce power to protect the battery).4. Can't Connect to Network, Wi-Fi Keeps Dropping
  • Mobile data works fine outside, but can't connect to Wi-Fi at home; or Wi-Fi is connected but there's no internet. Troubleshoot in this order:Toggle Airplane Mode
  • : Swipe down to Control Center, turn on Airplane Mode, wait 5 seconds, then turn it off. This is equivalent to making the phone search for the network again, very effective."Forget" Wi-Fi and reconnect

: Go to Wi-Fi settings, tap the exclamation mark next to the network name (gear icon on Android), select "Ignore This Network" or "Forget", then re-enter the password to connect.

Restart the router

  1. : Many people's home routers haven't been turned off for months, and over time they become unstable. Unplug the power, wait 30 seconds, then plug it back in—most Wi-Fi problems are solved.Check if it's the phone's problem
  2. : Do other devices connect to the same Wi-Fi normally? If they all work fine but your phone doesn't, the phone may need a restart or network settings reset (Settings → General → Transfer or Reset → Reset Network Settings—won't delete your data, but will clear all Wi-Fi passwords).5. Screen Issues: Unresponsive Touch, Flickering, Image Retention
  3. Unresponsive touch: First peel off the tempered glass film to see if it's the film's fault—cheap tempered films can indeed affect touch over time. Water on the screen or oil on your hands can also cause touch drift. If neither, restart and try again.
  4. Marks/ghost image on screen (burn-in): Displaying the same image for a long time (like keeping the screen on while browsing TikTok) will leave "ghost image" on OLED screens. This isn't screen damage, just temporary. Turning off the screen and resting for half an hour usually recovers it.

Screen flickering

  • : If it flickers at low brightness, it may be a PWM dimming issue, more common on OLED screens. Look for "DC dimming" or "anti-flicker" option in Settings—turning it on helps a lot. Not all phones have this feature.A completely dark/bright area on the screen
  • : This is more serious—likely physical screen damage, requiring screen replacement. Non-official repair screens usually have inferior color and brightness compared to originals, and also affect water resistance.6. Won't Turn On, Stuck at Logo—Don't Panic First
  • This situation is most likely to make your heart race, but stay calm and try these first:Charge for half an hour first
  • : Often the battery is just completely drained. Plug in the original charger, wait at least 30 minutes, then try to turn on. Some phones need to charge to a certain level before responding after being fully drained.Force restart

: For iPhone full-screen models, press volume up once, volume down once, then press and hold the side power button until the Apple Logo appears (may need to hold for 10-15 seconds). General Android method: press and hold the power button for 10+ seconds until vibration or screen lights up.

Stuck at boot screen, rebooting repeatedly

  • : This is called "white Apple" (iPhone) or "stuck at Logo" (Android). If force restart doesn't work, you may need to enter recovery mode and use a computer to repair. Connect iPhone to computer, open iTunes/Finder, enter recovery mode, then select "Update" (not "Restore")—this will reinstall the system but preserve data. For Android, enter Fastboot or Recovery mode; key combinations vary by brand, recommend searching your phone model + "enter recovery mode".If none of the above work
  • : Go to Wi-Fi settings, "Forget" your current Wi-Fi, re-enter password to connect.7. Sound Issues: Speaker Not Working, Low Call Volume
  • No speaker sound: First confirm it's not silent mode (iPhone side silent switch), Do Not Disturb mode, or volume turned all the way down. Sounds silly, but this accounts for 40% of cases. Then check whether Bluetooth is connected to a headphone or speaker.
  • Caller can't hear you: Check whether the microphone hole is blocked—the small hole at the bottom of the phone is easily blocked by dust. Clean gently with a soft brush. Don't poke hard with a needle or toothpick, you'll damage the dust mesh.

Distorted/cracking sound

  • : If caused by water in the speaker—don't use a hair dryer on hot! Use a paper towel to absorb surface moisture, then let it air dry naturally. Online suggestions of water-ejection apps (playing low-frequency sound to vibrate water out) have some effect, you can try.8. Finding Official Repair, Avoiding Pitfalls
  • If you've tried all the above methods and it still doesn't work, you need professional repair. But the repair market is full of pitfalls—let me share my own experiences and lessons learned:Find real official, not "looks official"
  • : Go to the brand's official website (Apple.com.cn, Huawei.com.cn, etc.) to find the "authorized service provider" list. Non-authorized shops on the street with an Apple logo may not use original parts—after repair, your water resistance is gone in a flash.Must-do before sending for repair

: Back up all data (don't assume data won't be lost during repair), log out of all important accounts (Apple ID, WeChat, Alipay), turn off "Find My Phone". Some repair shops will ask for your lock screen password, which has privacy risks—you'd better log out of accounts yourself before sending it over.

Screen replacement pitfalls

  • : Non-official screens come in "original-pressed" (original glass replaced), "aftermarket-pressed" (non-original glass), and "assembled" (all non-original). Prices differ by several times, but display quality and durability also differ a lot. If your phone is still under warranty, stick with official repair.Battery replacement pitfalls
  • : Non-original batteries may have falsely labeled capacity, and after half a year of use, degrade more than original batteries do in two years. Apple's official battery replacement price isn't much more expensive than non-official—recommend going official.Data recovery pitfalls
  • : If your phone gets water-damaged or broken, and the repair shop says "data recovery costs extra", be careful—some unscrupulous merchants will deliberately exaggerate the damage to charge more. Legitimate data recovery quotes a price first, then operates, and doesn't charge if recovery fails.The Universal First Move: Restart Your Phone
  • No matter what problem you encounter—lagging, crashing, can't connect to network, sound issues—first restart your phone. This sounds like a brush-off, but in my own experience, at least 60% of minor issues are resolved after a restart. Phones, like computers, accumulate all kinds of junk in memory over time—restart clears it and starts fresh. So next time your phone has issues, don't rush to search "what to do"—restart first, then see.Memorize Now: These Lifesaving Operations Should Be Second Nature
  • Force restart: Full-screen iPhone: press volume up → volume down → long press power button until Logo appears. Android: long press power button for 10-15 seconds until vibration.

Clean charging port

: Find a small tool (toothpick or SIM ejector pin), gently clean dust from the charging port.

Wi-Fi reconnect

  1. : Go to Wi-Fi settings, "Forget" your current Wi-Fi, re-enter password to connect.Toggle Airplane Mode
  2. : Swipe down to Control Center, turn on Airplane Mode, count to 5 in your head, turn it off, see if network recovers.Screenshot the steps for these operations, or write them in Notes. When problems arise, you don't need to frantically search—just flip through Notes.
  3. Chapter 20: Developer Mode and Advanced PermissionsThis chapter is for users who want to deeply explore the "hidden features" of their phone. Developer Mode, Root permissions, BL lock... these geeky-sounding concepts are actually not far from ordinary users.
  4. 1. Developer Mode: Unlock Hidden SettingsDeveloper Mode is a hidden menu built into the phone system, containing many features that ordinary users don't need but developers do.
  5. How to enable:

Android

: Go to Settings > About Phone > tap "Build Number" 7 times continuously, until it prompts "You are now in developer mode".

HarmonyOS

: Settings > About Phone > tap "HarmonyOS Version" 7 times continuously.

iOS
  • iOSCommon features:
  • USB Debugging: Connect to computer for advanced operations like flashing, data recovery.
  • Animation speed adjustment: Reduce or turn off animations to make the phone feel faster.
Commonly Used Features Overview:
  • : Display touch points on screen, suitable for recording tutorials.: A must-enable switch for connecting to a computer for advanced operations (such as flashing, data recovery, ADB commands). See the "ADB Practical Commands" section in this chapter.
  • : In some cases, improves smoothness.: Shows touch points on screen (a small dot following your finger), suitable for recording tutorials or demos.
Performance & Smoothness Related:
  • Animation Speed Adjustment (Window Animation Scale / Transition Animation Scale / Animator Duration Scale): These three options control the animation duration when opening apps and switching pages. The default is 1x; setting to 0.5x makes the phone "feel" faster (the actual program speed hasn't changed, just the animation is quicker); setting to off disables animations entirely. Most geeks set it to 0.5x — it preserves transition feel while seeming fast. Completely disabling animations can make operations feel abrupt and may mask real program stuttering, misleading you into thinking it's "very smooth."
  • Force GPU Rendering: Forces all 2D drawing to be processed by the GPU instead of the CPU. Can improve scrolling smoothness on older models or with poorly optimized apps, but also increases GPU load and power consumption. Modern phones already use GPU rendering extensively by default, so this toggle has limited impact on mid-to-high-end models — it's more of a legacy option. Ordinary users should keep the default.
  • Profile GPU Rendering: Displays a real-time bar chart on screen showing the rendering time of each frame. The green horizontal line represents 16.6ms (the frame time threshold for 60fps). Bars above the green line indicate dropped frames. This is a developer tool for troubleshooting app stuttering — ordinary users can also use it to compare which apps are poorly optimized. For example, if an app's bars frequently spike above the red line during scrolling, it's basically that app's fault.
Background & Battery Related:
  • Settings in Developer Mode may affect system stability—don't change options you don't understand. After enabling USB Debugging, be careful when connecting to computers, and don't connect to untrusted computers.: You can set "Standard limit," "At most 1 process," "At most 2 processes," etc. On the surface, limiting background processes seems like it would save battery, but Android's built-in background management is already quite good. Forcibly limiting it causes apps to reload frequently (cold starts actually consume more power and worsen the experience). This option is more suited for debugging — ordinary users shouldn't keep it enabled long-term; "Standard limit" is fine.
  • Don't Keep Activities: Destroys every activity as soon as you leave it. Highly discouraged — causes frequent white screens and reloads, only for testing app recovery logic.

Notes

: Prevents malicious software from being flashed into the system.

II. OEM Unlocking: The "Flashing Switch" in Developer Options

In Developer Options, there's an inconspicuous but important toggle — "OEM Unlocking" (some brands call it "Allow OEM Unlocking" or "Device Unlocking"). This toggle doesn't unlock the Bootloader itself — it's a "prerequisite permission": only when enabled will the manufacturer allow you to unlock the BL via fastboot commands or brand tools.

  • Purpose of the Toggle: Equivalent to declaring to the manufacturer "I agree to waive my warranty and accept the risks — please allow me to unlock the BL." If this toggle is off, any BL unlock command will be rejected outright.
  • Relationship with the BL Lock: OEM Unlocking is the "qualification application," while BL Unlock is the "actual operation." The former is just a tap in phone settings; the latter requires applying for an unlock code from the manufacturer's website and running fastboot commands on a computer (such as fastboot flashing unlock), and both are indispensable.
  • Does Factory Reset Reset It?: Yes. The "OEM Unlocking" toggle returns to off after a factory reset, but once the BL is unlocked, it's a physical-level state — a factory reset won't relock it. You need to manually execute fastboot flashing lock to relock it.
  • When Should You Enable It: Unless you're certain you want to flash or Root, keep it off. It and "USB Debugging" are independent toggles — both usually need to be enabled simultaneously when flashing.

Trivia: Why Do Manufacturers Include This Toggle

Early Android didn't have this toggle, so malware could silently flash the system as long as it got permissions. Google later required all Android manufacturers to include the "OEM Unlocking" toggle in Developer Options as a "user informed consent" confirmation. This is why even if you've unlocked the BL, reflashing will still fail if the OEM Unlocking toggle is turned off.

III. Bootloader Lock: The First Gate to Flashing

: Even if the phone is flashed, it can't be used without the original account password.

Warranty restriction
  • : Unlocking BL usually means losing official warranty.BL lock policies by brand:
  • Xiaomi: Can be unlocked, requires account binding waiting period (7-30 days).
  • Huawei: Stopped providing unlock codes after 2018, basically cannot be officially unlocked.
OnePlus
  • [Protect Privacy]OPPO/vivo
  • HuaweiSamsung
  • : Can be unlocked, but triggers Knox fuse, losing Samsung Pay and other features.Apple
  • [Install Apps from External Sources]3. Root Permission: Android's "Super Administrator"
  • SamsungBenefits of Root:
  • AppleUse advanced feature apps (like Titanium Backup, Greenify).

IV. ADB Practical Commands: Controlling Your Phone via Computer

ADB stands for Android Debug Bridge, an official Google command-line tool that lets a computer communicate with an Android phone via USB or Wi-Fi. It doesn't require Root — as long as the phone has "USB Debugging" enabled, you can use it. Think of it as a "remote control that sends commands from your computer to your phone" — flashing, installing apps, transferring files, checking logs, all rely on it.

How to Connect via USB:
  1. On the phone: Enter Developer Options → enable "USB Debugging."
  2. On the computer: Download Platform Tools from Google's official site (includes adb verb fastboot two executable files), extract to any directory.
  3. Connect the phone and computer with a data cable. The phone will show a popup "Allow USB debugging?" — check "Always allow" and confirm.
  4. In the computer's command line (Windows PowerShell or cmd), execute adb devices. If the output is similar to List of devices attached / xxxxxxxx device, the connection is successful.

Don't Ignore Driver and Authorization Popups

If Windows users see adb devices showing "unauthorized" or not listing the device at all, it's usually because the driver isn't installed properly or you forgot to tap "Allow" on the phone. Samsung/Xiaomi and other brands can install their respective "USB Drivers" or "Phone Assistant" to fix the driver; Mac and Linux generally don't need drivers. If you accidentally dismissed the phone popup, just unplug and replug the data cable and it will pop up again.

Commonly Used ADB Commands:
  • adb install app.apk: Installs an APK from the computer to the phone (-r means reinstall while keeping data;-s installs to SD card).
  • adb uninstall com.xxx.xxx: Uninstalls an app by package name.
  • adb push [computer path] /sdcard/[target path]: Pushes a file from the computer to the phone.
  • adb pull /sdcard/[file] [computer path]: Pulls a file from the phone to the computer (much faster than sending it to yourself on WeChat and downloading).
  • adb shell: Enters the phone's Linux shell, can directly execute lsandpmandam and other commands.
  • adb reboot bootloader: Reboots the phone into Fastboot mode (the entry point for flashing).
  • adb reboot recovery: Reboots into Recovery mode.
  • adb shell pm list packages: Lists all installed app package names on the phone (essential for finding package names). Add -s to see only system apps, add -3 to see only third-party apps.
  • adb shell pm uninstall --user 0 [package name]: Uninstalls pre-installed apps for the current user — no Root required. See the practical guide below.
Practical Guide: Uninstalling Pre-installed Apps Without Root:

This is one of ADB's most practical features: using the pm uninstall --user 0 command, you can uninstall pre-installed apps for the "current user" without Root and without affecting the system partition. Uninstalled apps "disappear" from the system but are actually still in the system partition — they'll come back after a factory reset.

  1. First use adb shell pm list packages -s to list all system apps and find the package name you want to uninstall. For example, Xiaomi Browser is com.android.browser, and Huawei AppGallery is com.vmall.clientTrivia: What is README
  2. Not sure which app a package name corresponds to? You can use adb shell pm list packages | findstr [keyword] to search on the computer, or install a third-party app "Package Viewer" on the phone to directly view each app's package name.
  3. Execute the uninstall:adb shell pm uninstall --user 0 [package name]. For example, adb shell pm uninstall --user 0 com.android.browser. If it returns Success , it's successful.
  4. Want to restore? Two methods: ① Factory reset (most thorough but cumbersome); ② Reinstall:adb shell cmd package install-existing [package name]Trivia: What is README

Never Delete Critical System Packages

Although "pm uninstall --user 0" is a safe method that doesn't require Root, deleting critical system apps (such as com.android.systemui status bar,com.android.phone phone,com.android.settings settings) can cause serious problems like system crashes, black screens, and inability to boot. Before deleting, Google "can this package name be deleted" — better to delete less than to delete wrong. Recommend deleting only one or two at a time and confirming everything is fine before continuing.

Trivia: What Does --user 0 Mean?

Android 4.2+ supports multi-user, where each user has an independent ID (the owner is 0, additional users start from 10).--user 0 means "uninstall for the current owner only" — the APK file in the system partition still exists, it's just not shown to the owner. That's why it doesn't need Root — it doesn't touch system files, it just changes the "user configuration." This is also the biggest difference from Root uninstalling: Root uninstalling actually deletes from the system, so no user has it anymore; ADB uninstalling just "hides it for the current user."

V. Root Access: Android's "Super Administrator"

Root access is equivalent to the superuser in Linux (full control over the / directory, can read/write any file), the highest privilege level in Android. It fundamentally differs from Windows Administrator: Windows imposes many restrictions on administrators for security (the true highest privilege is actually TrustedInstaller), and even Administrator can't directly execute like Linux root can. sudo rm -rf /*. After obtaining Root access, you can modify system files, uninstall pre-installed apps, and use advanced apps that require Root.

VI. SafetyNet and Play Integrity Certification: Why Bank Apps Don't Work After Root

Many Root users have experienced this devastating moment: after Rooting and excitedly installing a bunch of modules, you open your bank app — "Your device is insecure and cannot be used," Google Pay doesn't work, and even Netflix refuses HD playback. Behind this is Google's two device integrity certification mechanisms: the older SafetyNet and the newer Play Integrity API.

What Are SafetyNet / Play Integrity:
  • SafetyNet Attestation (Legacy, since 2017): Google's early device integrity check API, where apps query Google servers to check "whether this device passed CTS compatibility testing and is in an unmodified official state." Results are divided into Basic Attestation and Strong Attestation (relies on hardware keys). Google has announced that SafetyNet will be gradually deprecated after 2024.
  • Play Integrity API (New, since 2022): Google's replacement, stricter and more comprehensive than SafetyNet. In addition to device integrity, it includes "app integrity" (whether the app has been tampered with) and "account/licensing integrity" (whether the user account is trusted by Google). New apps should migrate to Play Integrity.
  • Who Uses It: Banking, financial, and payment apps (such as Google Pay, various banks' mobile banking, some scenarios of Alipay/WeChat Pay), streaming media (Netflix HD copyright protection), some game anti-cheat (such as some Tencent/NetEase games), enterprise office apps (MDM device compliance checks).
Play Integrity's Three Certification Levels:
  • MEETS_DEVICE_INTEGRITY: The device runs genuine Android, Bootloader is locked, no Root, CTS compatibility test passed. Banking and payment apps work normally.
  • MEETS_BASIC_INTEGRITY: The device is basically trustworthy, but may have minor anomalies. Some apps will degrade (e.g., Netflix still plays but limits resolution), some strict bank apps will refuse outright.
  • MEETS_STRONG_INTEGRITY: The highest level, requires hardware key endorsement (such as the Titan M chip in Google Pixel series). Most third-party brand devices can't reach this level even without Root.
  • No Label (NO_INTEGRITY): The device is Rooted, BL is unlocked, a third-party ROM is flashed, or it's identified as an emulator. The vast majority of payment/banking apps will refuse to run.
Why Do These Apps Fail After Root:

Apps initiate certification requests to Google servers through the Play Integrity API. Google checks multiple device indicators — Bootloader lock status, whether the system partition has been modified, whether su binary files exist, whether SELinux is in permissive mode, etc. Any anomaly causes the returned certification level to be lowered or empty, and bank apps see "device insecure" and naturally refuse service.

Modern Hiding Solutions: Magisk Hide / Shamiko / Zygisk:

To enjoy Root convenience while still using banking apps, the community has developed a series of solutions to "hide the Root state." The core idea is the same: make the detection program see a "normal-looking" device instead of a modified system.

  • : Old-school Root solution, currently no longer updated.: The current mainstream Systemless Root solution — doesn't modify the system partition, but achieves Root through mounting. The benefit of this design is a lower chance of OTA update failure and cleaner uninstall. It's the foundation for all subsequent hiding solutions. However, using Magisk still requires unlocking the BL.
  • Magisk Hide (Discontinued): Magisk's early built-in hiding module, could hide Root from specified apps. But since 2021 it was removed by Magisk officially, because Google continuously upgraded detection methods, and the two sides fell into a "cat-and-mouse game."
  • Zygisk: A new mechanism introduced in Magisk 24.0+, similar to Riru, injects into the Zygote process to load modules, more stealthy than directly modifying the system. Enabling Zygisk is a prerequisite for using modern hiding solutions.
  • Shamiko: The current mainstream hiding module, works with Zygisk, can hide Root for specified apps ("reverse whitelist" mode), hide Magisk itself, and fake the Bootloader lock status. Shamiko is distributed through the LSPosed repository or GitHub.
  • Play Integrity Fix（osm0sis）: A Magisk module specifically targeting Google Play Integrity detection, modifies the device fingerprint to make Google think your device is an unrooted official model.

The Cat-and-Mouse Game Never Ends

Google updates detection rules periodically, and app developers follow up with Play Integrity upgrades. A hiding solution that works today may be detected tomorrow. If you fully rely on banking/payment apps (such as daily transfers, QR code payments), the safest choice remains: don't Root, don't unlock the BL. Hiding solutions are more suitable for a "main phone without Root + backup phone for Root experimentation" enthusiast setup.

VII. Advice for Ordinary Users

  • : Not recommended for ordinary users—risks outweigh benefits. If you really need certain features, first look into whether there are alternatives that don't require Root.: You can enable it to experience animation acceleration, GPU rendering analysis, and other features, but don't randomly change other options you don't understand.
  • OEM Unlocking and BL Lock: If you don't plan to flash or Root, keep both toggles in their default (off) state for maximum safety.
  • ADB: A powerful no-Root tool that ordinary people can use too — for example, using pm uninstall --user 0 to uninstall pre-installed apps. But before deleting, always check whether the package name can be safely deleted.
  • A security lock added by manufacturers; it must be unlocked before flashing custom firmware.: Root is not recommended for ordinary users — the risks outweigh the benefits. If you truly need certain features, first check whether there are no-Root alternatives (such as using ADB to uninstall pre-installed apps, or using Shizuku to replace some Root functionality).

But have you ever thought about how often your chat records, payment passwords, photos... these pieces of information are "running naked" online? Honestly, most people never think about this question, but once something goes wrong—such as your account being stolen or your bank card being swiped—it's too late to regret. In this chapter, let's talk about how to make your digital life less "transparent."1. VPN: The "Invisibility Cloak" in the Network

IV. Beyond (Chapters 21-26)

Regular internet access

Chapter 21: In-depth Exploration of Mobile Networks and Information Security

Using a VPN

: Your phone → VPN encrypted tunnel → VPN server → target website. The data is encrypted and encapsulated, so "peeping toms" can only see a bunch of garbled text. Additionally, the target website sees the IP address of the VPN server, not your real IP.

So what can a VPN actually do? Simply put: first,

  • protect your privacy on public Wi-Fi; second,
  • bypass geographical restrictions(such as watching content only available in certain countries); third,

prevent your Internet Service Provider (ISP) from logging your browsing habits. But I must remind you:don't use free VPNs!Free often means your data is their "commodity." I have a friend who used a free VPN, and his phone started popping up ads for no reason. Later we found out that the VPN had packaged and sold his browsing data to advertisers. So when choosing a VPN, either choose a paid big brand (like NordVPN, ExpressVPN), or simply don't use one.Also, VPN is not omnipotent. It can only protect data "in transit." If the target website itself is insecure, or your phone already has malware, a VPN can't help you.2. The "Sweet Trap" of Public Wi-Fi—More Dangerous Than You ThinkYou might think, it's just connecting to free Wi-Fi, how much risk can there be? Let me tell you a true story: security researchers once did an experiment where they set up a Wi-Fi hotspot called "Starbucks_Free" at an airport, and within an hour, over a hundred people connected. In reality, this hotspot was set up by the researchers themselves, and allunencrypted trafficpassing through this hotspot—such as the content of HTTP web pages you visit and App communications without TLS enabled—they could indeed intercept and view.

But note a key premise: today, the WeChat, online banking, and Alipay you use daily have mostly already adopted HTTPS encryption. In other words, even if attackers intercept the data packets, what they see is just a bunch of garbled text, and they

cannot directly read your chat content or payment password

. However, they can still know which websites you visited (domains). If certain old Apps or web pages are still using HTTP plaintext transmission, the content will be completely exposed. This type of attack is called a "Man-in-the-Middle" attack, and the principle is that the attacker "inserts themselves" between you and the real Wi-Fi router. What's more frightening is that many people's phones are set to "automatically connect to known Wi-Fi." Attackers only need to set their hotspot name to one you've connected to before (such as "ChinaNet" or "CMCC"), and your phone will automatically connect to it.So how to defend against this? Here are a few practical suggestions:Look for HTTPS

: The address bar starts with https://, and the extra "s" stands for Secure. When accessing any website that requires a password, if you see http:// (without the s), stop immediately and don't enter anything! Now mainstream browsers will display an "insecure" warning before non-HTTPS websites, so be alert when you see this mark.Turn off "auto-connect": Whether iPhone or Android, turn off "auto-join" or "auto-connect" in Wi-Fi settings. Rather than letting your phone judge for itself, manually tap each time.

Use mobile data for sensitive operations

  • : Transfers, logging into online banking, entering ID numbers... honestly use your own 4G/5G data for these operations, don't save that little bit of data.Forget infrequently used Wi-Fi
  • : After returning from a business trip or travel, "forget" all the hotel Wi-Fi and airport Wi-Fi you temporarily connected to before. This way, next time your phone won't automatically connect to a fake hotspot with the same name.3. How Does HTTPS Protect You?—SSL/TLS Handshake
  • I just mentioned HTTPS, so how does it actually work? Every time you visit an HTTPS website, an "SSL/TLS handshake" occurs between the browser and the server. The whole process goes something like this:Your browser says: "Hey, server, I want to communicate securely with you, here's my list of encryption capabilities (supported encryption algorithms, etc.)."
  • The server replies: "Okay, I've selected this set of encryption schemes from your list, here's my digital certificate, which contains my public key, signed and certified by a certain CA organization."The browser verifies the certificate's authenticity: Was it issued by a trusted CA? Has it expired? Does the domain name match?

After verification passes, both parties use public key encryption to negotiate a "session key," and all subsequent communication is encrypted with this key.

This is like going to a bank to do business: you first hand over your ID card (certificate), the teller verifies your identity, then the two of you agree on a secret code, and subsequent conversations can only be understood by the two of you. Even if someone eavesdrops nearby, they can only hear encrypted garbled text.

  1. But note: HTTPS only guarantees that the "transmission process" is encrypted, not that the target website is a good actor. Phishing websites can also use HTTPS—that little lock icon only indicates that you're connected to "some website," not that the website is the one you want to visit. So you still need to verify the URL yourself.
  2. 4. DNS Security: Is Your "Network Phonebook" Safe?
  3. DNS (Domain Name System) is like the internet's phonebook: you type "baidu.com," and DNS helps you look up which IP address it corresponds to (such as 110.242.68.66), and then the browser can connect. The problem is that traditional DNS queries are
  4. plaintext

and

not encrypted

! This means your ISP, Wi-Fi provider, or any intermediate node can see which websites you've visited.

What's even more disgusting is "DNS hijacking": attackers tamper with the DNS process to point "baidu.com" to a fake phishing website. You clearly typed the correct URL, but you're taken to an identical but actually fake login page, and once you enter your account password, you're done for.Fortunately, there are now encrypted DNS solutions:DNS over HTTPS (DoH): Hides DNS queries in HTTPS traffic, mixed in with normal web browsing traffic, making it impossible to distinguish which ones are DNS queries.DNS over TLS (DoT)

: Uses the TLS encryption protocol to specifically protect DNS queries, with an independent port. Network administrators can know you're using DoT but can't see the content.

I personally recommend using Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1 or Google's 8.8.8.8 as DNS servers; both support encrypted DNS. In Android's "Private DNS" setting, just enter "one.one.one.one" or "dns.google," super simple. iPhone is a bit more troublesome, requiring you to install a profile or set it up through an App, but it's worth doing.

  • 5. Does "Incognito Browsing" Really Make You Invisible?First, the conclusion:
  • Incognito mode is your window curtain, not an invisibility cloak.What it does: It doesn't leave traces locally—after closing the incognito window, the browser doesn't save your browsing history, cookies, form fill-in records, or search history. It's appropriate to use incognito mode when looking something up on someone else's computer or buying a gift without family members finding out from browsing records.

What it can't do:

The website you visit

: When closed, it's the size of a regular phone; when opened, it's nearly square like a small tablet. Representatives: Huawei Mate X series, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold series, Xiaomi MIX Fold series, vivo X Fold series. Main selling point: "one phone = phone + tablet".; your IP address, device information, and browsing behavior are clear on the website's end.

Your network operator

can still see which websites you visited

  • , just not the specific content (if HTTPS is used).Company/school network administratorscan also monitor
  • your internet behavior.Files you download and bookmarks you add willbe retained
  • and won't disappear when you close the window.So remember: Incognito mode is a "local eraser," not a "network invisibility cloak." If you really need to hide your internet traces, you need a combination punch like VPN + Tor browser, but for daily use, knowing this much is enough.6. Browser Privacy: Don't Let the Browser Sell You Out
  • You may not realize that the browser itself is a huge information collector. Cookies, browsing history, cache, autofill, location permissions... each one could leak your privacy. A few suggestions:Clean browsing data regularly: Every once in a while, go to settings and clean out cookies, cache, and history. Not to prevent "being tracked"—that's no longer very effective by clearing cookies—but to prevent your phone from getting slower and slower. Browser cache can take up several GB of space.

Give up the "Do Not Track" fantasy

: The "Send 'Do Not Track' request" option in browsers is essentially "asking" websites not to track you. But whether websites listen is another matter entirely; most websites simply ignore it. Don't count on it.

Make good use of privacy-protecting browsers

: A three-step pipeline of speech recognition (ASR) → machine translation (NMT) → speech synthesis (TTS), with end-to-end latency now controllable within 1 second.

Scenario 2: AI Erase—Saving Tourist Photos "Ruined" by Passersby

Actual performance: Took a beautiful selfie at a scenic spot, but the background is crowded with other tourists? Use "Magic Erase" to circle the passersby, and the phone will automatically identify and "erase" them, then intelligently fill in the background. The results are often stunning.

Underlying principle: The image segmentation (Inpainting) model first identifies and deletes the selected area, then "imagines" reasonable fill content based on surrounding pixels and semantic understanding. The AI model behind this is trained on millions of images.

Scenario 3: AI Photo Editing—One-Click to Become a "Photography Master"

Actual performance: Took a gray, hazy landscape photo on a cloudy day? AI "Magic Sky" can one-click replace the sky with clear sky, sunset, or even starry sky. AI image expansion can turn a vertical composition into a horizontal one, with the phone "imagining" scenes beyond the frame.

Underlying principle: Based on Generative AI's Diffusion Model, it understands the semantic content of the image and then generates new pixels. This is the "cutting edge" of current AI image processing.

Scenario 4: Document Processing—An Efficiency Multiplier for Office Workers

Actual performance: After a meeting, throw the meeting recording to AI, and it can automatically organize structured meeting minutes, extract action items, and generate summaries. A 10-page English PDF report can be distilled by AI in 10 seconds to give you the core conclusions.

Underlying principle: Long Context LLMs can "read through" documents of tens of thousands of words, performing multi-round reasoning and information extraction. Apple Intelligence, Huawei Xiaoyi, WPS AI, Tencent Yuanbao, etc., all have this capability.

Scenario 5: AI Image Search and Object Recognition—Your "Visual Search Engine"

Actual performance: See an unfamiliar flower on the street, open the camera, and AI immediately tells you "This is a hibiscus." Looking through your album for photos taken at the beach last year, search for "ocean," and AI automatically finds all photos containing the sea, without manual scrolling.

Underlying principle: Computer Vision (CV) models vectorize (Embedding) image content, then match it with text queries for similarity. This "multimodal search" is a major leap in phone album management.

  2. In the previous two chapters, we built a secure "boundary wall" for our phones and witnessed its increasingly smart "AI brain" within the wall. Now, let's unlock one of the phone's ultimate potentials: letting it "think" like a programmer and automatically complete the continuous tasks you set. You might say: "I don't know how to write code, what does this have to do with me?" What Exactly Is Automation?
  3. In plain language, automation is:letting your phone automatically do a series of things for you when a certain condition is met.

Case 2: Complete Phone Replacement Data Migration

  • Scenario: iPhone 13 → Xiaomi 15 cross-brand phone replacement.
  • Steps: ① Old phone iCloud/WeChat built-in backup → ② Sign out of Apple ID + turn off "Find" → ③ New phone uses "Xiaomi Migration" app to scan QR code → ④ Select migration items → ⑤ WeChat uses built-in "Chat History Migration" separately → ⑥ Verify key data (contacts/photos/WeChat) → ⑦ Old phone encrypted wipe.
  • Expected Result: Zero data loss, old phone can be safely resold.

Chapter 23: Programming Thinking and Automation Enlightenment

For example: every morning when you wake up, you manually turn off Do Not Disturb mode, open WeChat to check messages, open the weather App to see what to wear today, and open NetEase Cloud Music to play a song. If you package these steps into an automated flow, set it to "automatically execute at 7 AM every day," then when you wake up, you just need to pick up your phone, and everything is already prepared. Doesn't it feel great just thinking about it?

Automation is essentially the "if... then..." logic chain, the if-else in programming. Once you understand this way of thinking, even if you never write code in your life, your problem-solving organization will be much stronger. Core elements:

Trigger condition: When to start? It can be "every morning at 7 AM," "when I connect to home Wi-Fi," "when I arrive at a certain location," "when phone battery is below 20%." Action to execute

: What specifically to do? It can be sending a WeChat message, opening an App, adjusting volume, switching wallpaper, playing music, sending notifications... almost everything you can do manually on your phone, automation can do.

Intermediate logic

  1. (optional but powerful): If situation A, do X; otherwise do Y. For example, "if it's a workday, play news podcast; on weekends, play music"—this is called conditional branching.2. iOS "Shortcuts"—The Automation Magic Tool for Apple Users
  2. Apple's "Shortcuts" App is a built-in application that doesn't need to be downloaded. Its core concept is to put various operations together like building blocks. First, let's cover a few key concepts:"Shortcut"
  3. : A complete automation flow that can be manually tapped to run, or triggered by Siri voice. For example, you say "Hey Siri, going home mode," and it automatically executes a series of operations you've set up."Automation"

: Instructions that run automatically based on trigger conditions, without needing you to manually trigger them. For example, "when the phone connects to car Bluetooth, automatically open the Maps App." Automations are set up under the "Automation" tab, separate from "Shortcuts."

"Action"

  • : The smallest execution unit. Opening an App is an action, sending a message is an action, getting weather is an action, adjusting brightness is an action. You can chain hundreds or thousands of actions together.Let me show you a few genuinely useful examples; you'll understand after following along:
  • Example 1: One-Click "Good Morning Routine"Every morning, tap once (or say "Good morning" to Siri), and the phone will automatically: get today's weather → read out the weather and temperature → show today's calendar schedule → open your frequently used music App to start playing. Steps: Create new shortcut → add action "Get Current Weather" → add "Speak Text" → add "Get Calendar Events" → add "Show Reminder" → add "Open App" and select NetEase Cloud Music. It's that simple, all drag-and-drop.
  • Example 2: Automatic "Power Saving Mode"In the "Automation" tab, create new automation → select "Battery Level" → set "below 30%" → add actions "Set Low Power Mode to On," "Reduce Screen Brightness to 30%," "Turn off Bluetooth." From now on, when phone battery drops below 30%, it automatically enters power saving mode without you worrying about it.

Example 3: Scan Code Automatic Bookkeeping

Every time you scan a code to pay with WeChat/Alipay, the phone reads the payment notification and automatically records the amount and merchant to a memo or Numbers spreadsheet. This requires using the "Receive SMS/Notification" trigger in Shortcuts' "Automation" (iOS 17+ supports reading Wallet transactions), combined with the "Append to Numbers" action. For people who want to keep accounts but are too lazy to do it manually, this is a lifesaver.

There's also a clever use many people don't know about: you can add shortcuts to your home screen, turning them into an App icon. For example, make a "Call a Ride Home" shortcut, put the icon on the desktop, and with one tap, it directly opens Didi and sets the destination to home—much faster than opening the App yourself and slowly typing.

3. Android Automation—Tasker and Its Friends

On the Android side, things are a bit more complicated, but the ceiling is also higher. Let's start with the simple ones:

Entry Level: Auto Clicker

Many Android phones come with "Auto Clicker" built-in, or you can download it from the app store. Its principle is super simple: you manually operate once, it records the coordinates and time intervals of your taps, then can play them back at high speed. For example, if a certain App gives daily check-in rewards, you record the tapping process once, and then it automatically runs every day. The downside is: it only recognizes coordinates; if the interface layout changes (such as a pop-up ad), it taps the wrong place.

Intermediate Level: Tasker—The King of Android Automation

Tasker is universally recognized as the most powerful automation tool on the Android platform, consistently topping the charts. Honestly, its learning curve is a bit steep and the interface isn't pretty, but once you get the hang of it, you'll feel your phone suddenly becomes omnipotent. Tasker's core is also the "trigger → task" pattern:

Profile

: Defines "when to trigger." Trigger conditions can be time, location, Wi-Fi connection status, Bluetooth connection, receiving specific notifications, battery status, screen orientation... Tasker supports an absurd number of trigger conditions, dozens of them.

Task

: Defines "what to do after triggering." A task can contain multiple actions, executed in order. Action types include: adjusting system settings (volume, brightness, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, airplane mode), sending SMS, HTTP requests, executing Shell commands, controlling media playback, popping up dialogs, and so on.

Here are some classic practical Tasker scenarios:

  • Auto-turn on Wi-Fi when arriving home: Set the trigger condition to "connect to specific cell tower" (because you'll connect to a fixed tower near your home) → task "Turn on Wi-Fi." No GPS needed and no power consumption; the phone automatically turns on Wi-Fi as soon as it enters the community area.
  • Meeting mode: Trigger condition "calendar event title contains 'meeting'" → task "Set silent mode, turn off media volume, auto-reply to WeChat (requires plugin support)." Never worry about your phone suddenly ringing during a meeting again.

Late-night eye protection

  • : Trigger condition "time 22:00-06:00" → task "Turn on eye protection mode, reduce brightness to 20%, set screen to black and white (grayscale mode)." Black and white screen has a miraculous effect on the desire to scroll short videos—once the picture goes gray, you don't want to scroll anymore.Auto-play podcast when headphones inserted
  • : Trigger condition "wired headphones inserted/Bluetooth headphones connected" → task "Open Xiaoyuzhou App and start playing the latest episode." Put on headphones and start listening, without unlocking the phone to find the App.If you find Tasker too hard to learn, try its simplified sibling:
  • MacroDroid. The interface is much friendlier, with rich templates, suitable for users who don't want to tinker. Also, many domestic Android systems (Xiaomi's MIUI, Huawei's HarmonyOS, OPPO's ColorOS) now come with "Scenes" or "Smart Assistant" features; while not as powerful as Tasker, they're completely sufficient for daily automation.
  • 4. Daily Applications of Automation ThinkingThe biggest gain from learning automation is actually not saving that little bit of time, but

changing the way you think about problems. Once you're used to the "if X happens, automatically do Y" thinking pattern, you'll find that a large number of repetitive tasks in life can be eliminated. For example:After taking photos each time, automatically back up to cloud storage and then compress local photos to small sizes to save space.

Every morning, automatically read today's schedule from the calendar and generate a text message sent to family via WeChat.

After receiving a delivery sign-off SMS, automatically add a "pick up package" to-do in the memo.When the phone is fully charged, automatically send a voice reminder to unplug the charger (to avoid overcharging damage to the battery).Every day at quitting time, if still near the company (through cell tower positioning), automatically remind "time to get off work."

  • These sound advanced, but actually, as long as you master the two basic concepts of "trigger + action," combined with Shortcuts or Tasker, you can make them all. The key is
  • you first need to realize "this thing can be automated"
  • —many people don't lack the ability, they just never think in that direction.

  • Automation isn't all smooth sailing; I've stepped into a few pitfalls for you first:

Location triggers may not work reliably: iOS's "arrive/leave location" trigger uses geofencing technology, and accuracy depends on GPS signal and system optimization. Sometimes it triggers only 10 minutes after you've arrived home. It's recommended to use Wi-Fi connection or cell tower triggers instead of location triggers—more reliable and more power-efficient.Shortcuts "Automation" requires authorization

: In iOS, most triggers under the "Automation" tab require manual confirmation to run (iOS's security mechanism). However, Wi-Fi connection, Bluetooth connection, and alarm stopped triggers can run fully automatically without confirmation.

Tasker requires accessibility permission

  • : Many advanced features (such as simulating taps) require accessibility service permission, which makes the phone display a persistent notification in settings. This is Android's security design and can't be removed.Don't make automation too complicated
  • : When starting automation, begin with small flows of "2-3 actions." Don't jump straight into a 20-step super flow—you'll go crazy debugging it.Tip: The Right Posture for Getting Started with Automation
  • First spend 5 minutes thinking: What are the top 3 things you repeat most on your phone every day? For example, your morning routine, your habits after connecting Bluetooth headphones, your settings before going out... Start with these high-frequency small things and make a simple automation for each. Even if each automation only saves you 5 seconds, it adds up over time. And the sense of accomplishment after making them is truly addictive.Practice: Three Beginner Automation Challenges

based on Git. It launched in 2008, was acquired by Microsoft in 2018, and remains the world's largest open-source code hosting platform, hosting hundreds of millions of repositories covering almost all mainstream programming languages.

Many people confuse these two terms when first encountering them; let me clarify for you:Comparison ItemGit

GitHub

Version control tool (software)

Code hosting platform (website) Running location On local computer

GitHub's Core Concepts and Features 📁 Basic Concepts

Before getting started, first get to know a few high-frequency words, otherwise you'll be confused when looking at GitHub's interface:Repository (Repo for short): One project corresponds to one repository, which stores all the code files, historical versions, and documentation for that project. You can think of it as a "project folder."

Commit

: A record of one modification to the code. Each Commit comes with a description, recording "what was changed this time, why it was changed." This is the foundation of Git/GitHub's ability to "time travel."

Branch

  • : An independent development line split from the main line. For example, if you want to add a new feature, you can open a branch to develop separately, and merge it back to the main line after development, without affecting others.Clone
  • : Copy a complete version of the cloud repository to your local computer, after which you can modify the code locally.Push/Pull
  • : Push is uploading local code to GitHub, Pull is downloading the latest code from GitHub to local. These are the two core actions for syncing code during team collaboration.Pull Request (PR for short)
  • : When you've finished modifying code on a branch and want to merge it into the main branch, you initiate a PR, letting team members review the code before merging. This is GitHub's core collaboration mechanism.Issue
  • : Used to record bugs, feature requests, and discussion topics. Each Issue is like a discussion thread, where you can assign responsible persons and add labels.Fork
  • : Copy someone else's repository to your own account, where you can modify your copy freely without affecting the original repository. After modifications, you can send a PR to the original author, requesting to merge your improvements.🛠️ Core Features
  • GitHub provides more than just code storage, including:Version control
  • : Records the history of every code change; if you break the code, you can always return to the last working version.Team collaboration
: Supports parallel development of the same project by multiple users; multiple people developing simultaneously won't overwrite or conflict.

Issue tracking

  • : Use Issues to record bugs and feature requests, making it easy for teams to follow up.Project management
  • : Integrates to-do items, project boards (Projects), and other management tools, equivalent to a built-in lightweight Trello.Automation
  • : ThroughGitHub Actions
  • , achieve automatic compilation, testing, packaging, and deployment after code submission—the core tool of modern "CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment)."Documentation management
  • : README introduces the project, Wiki stores detailed architecture and development standards, and Pages can even directly host static websites.Code hosting and display: Each repository has a beautiful web display with syntax highlighting—it's the "front door" of your technical work.Open source community
  • : You can Star (favorite) projects you like, Watch (follow) project updates, Follow (follow) developers, and participate in global open source collaboration.4. Registration and Getting Started: Create Your First Repository in Five Minutes
