  4. This chapter is an in-depth expansion of Chapter 20, suitable for users who want to truly understand the underlying mechanisms of phones or even try flashing. Please note that these operations carry certain risks, so proceed with caution.1. Deep Understanding of BootloaderBootloader is the first program to run when the phone starts; its task is to initialize hardware and load the operating system kernel. You can think of Bootloader as the phone's "gatekeeper."
  5. How BL Lock Works:

Verify signature

: BL lock verifies the digital signature of the boot image; only manufacturer-signed systems can boot.

Prevent downgrade

: Prevents users from flashing older system versions to exploit known vulnerabilities.

Protect data
  • : Even if a new system is flashed, user data cannot be accessed without the original account password.2. Detailed Process for Unlocking BL Lock (Using Xiaomi as an Example)
  • Apply for unlock permission: Apply for unlocking on the Xiaomi Unlock Tool website.
  • Bind account: Bind your Xiaomi account in phone settings.
🔐 Hardware-Level Storage and Verification

The BL lock status (Locked/Unlocked) and the manufacturer's public key are typically stored in protected hardware areas (such as Qualcomm's devinfo partition, eFuse, or RPMB partition) to prevent software tampering. On each boot, the Bootloader reads the status from this secure area and decides whether to perform strict signature verification.

🔏 Digital Signature Verification

When manufacturers release system updates or images, they sign them with their private keys. At device boot, the Bootloader verifies the system images (such as boot.img, recovery.img) using the built-in public key. The process works as follows:

  1. Recalculate the hash value of the system image.
  2. Decrypt the image's built-in signature with the public key to obtain a hash value.
  3. Compare the two hash values — if they match, verification passes. This ensures the system image hasn't been tampered with by third parties.
🔗 Secure Boot Chain

The BL lock is the first link in the entire secure boot chain. Only after it passes verification does it load and execute the next stage bootloader (such as the kernel), ensuring the trustworthiness of the system boot environment layer by layer.

📊 Locked vs. Unlocked: The Dual Impact of BL Lock

To more intuitively understand the pros and cons of the BL lock, here's a comparison table showing its impact across 5 core dimensions:

Core Role Locked State (Default) Unlocked State
System Security Prevents flashing unsigned unofficial systems, protects system integrity and low-level security
✅ High security: only loads officially signed images, effectively resists malicious firmware tampering		 ⚠️ Reduced security: allows flashing third-party ROMs, system integrity verification fails, malware with Root access can deeply tamper with the system
System Stability Ensures the phone runs the manufacturer-tested and optimized official system, guaranteeing stability and smoothness
✅ Stable: uses official firmware, complete features, reliable OTA updates		 ⚠️ Increased risk: third-party ROMs may have compatibility issues, potentially causing system crashes, bricking, hardware function anomalies (such as camera, fast charging), OTA update failures
Warranty Rights Manufacturers provide warranty service by locking BL to ensure a stable official system
✅ Warranty valid: enjoy official free warranty service (non-artificial damage)		 ⚠️ Warranty void: most manufacturers consider BL unlocking as voluntarily waiving warranty. Even if relocked, historical unlock records may be detected and warranty refused
Data Security The unlock process usually forces data wipe to prevent old data from being maliciously exploited in the new system environment
✅ Data security: in daily use, BL lock limits the ability of malware to modify the system partition		 ⚠️ Data risk: unlocking forcibly wipes all user data; if not properly encrypted after unlocking, data storage may be insecure; data is easier to extract via flashing if lost
Feature Limitations Ensures security-dependent features (such as payment, banking apps) work normally
✅ Complete features: all official features work normally		 ⚠️ Feature limited: some security-sensitive apps (such as Google Pay, banking apps) may refuse to run upon detecting BL unlock status; DRM services may be downgraded, affecting HD video playback

V. Samsung Knox: The Irreversible Cost of BL Unlocking

Unlike other Android manufacturers, Samsung's BL unlock mechanism has a unique "fuse" design:For Samsung phones, unlocking triggers Knox fuse tripping, permanently losing some security features (such as Samsung Pay); clears all protected data; affects warranty. Specifically:

  • The Fuse Is One-Time: There's an eFuse inside the phone that permanently burns out once it detects BL has been unlocked — it cannot be restored.
  • Affected Features: Samsung Pay (transit cards/bank cards), Knox Secure Folder, enterprise MDM management, and some health insurance apps will all stop working.
  • Forced Data Wipe: After the fuse is triggered, the phone forces a factory reset — all local data is erased (cloud data is not affected).
  • Warranty Impact: Officially stated that after Knox fuse is tripped, warranty service is no longer available.

Think Twice Before Proceeding

Samsung's Knox fuse tripping isirreversible— once triggered, you can't go back to the original factory state. If you just want to use some features that originally require Root, first check whether there are no-Root alternatives.

Payment function abnormalities

Before flashing, be sure to make a complete backup, carefully read the tutorial, and confirm that the model and version match.

Q1: Can BL Unlock Be Reversed?

Chapter 25: Second-hand Phone Disposal and Digital Legacy

Execute ultimate "formatting"

: Modern phones' "factory reset" usually includes encrypted erasure.

Core principle: Data cleaning isn't "deletion" — it's "overwriting." Many people think dragging photos to the trash and clearing the album is enough, but after the phone changes hands, the new owner can scan with data recovery software and recover old photos, chat history, and ID photos — this kind of "social death" happens every year.

  1. : After factory reset, fill storage with junk files, then perform another factory reset.: Complete the last full backup, sign out of all accounts (iCloud, Huawei/Xiaomi/Samsung account, Google account), turn off "Find My Phone" — otherwise the next user will be blocked by Activation Lock.
  2. Apple "Legacy Contact": Modern phones' "factory reset" usually includes encrypted wiping — it destroys the encryption key itself. Once the key is gone, all data on the disk instantly becomes garbled.
  3. Final "Camouflage" (Only for Old Devices): Modern phones (iOS 8+, Android 6+) already have full disk encryption (FBE) by default. Factory reset destroys the encryption key — data is theoretically unrecoverable,this step is not needed. Only for very old non-encrypted devices (pre-2015), after factory reset, should you fill the storage with junk files and then perform another factory reset.

Brand-Specific Data Wipe Quick Reference Table: Although the principles are the same, each brand hides "factory reset" in slightly different locations. Key differences are below.

Brand Wipe Entry Point Key Differences & Notes
Huawei Settings > System & Updates > Reset > Factory Reset Must sign out of Huawei account and turn off "Find My Phone" first, otherwise Activation Lock will trigger; may require password verification in Pure Mode.
Xiaomi / Redmi Settings > My Device > Factory Reset At the bottom, there are "Format Virtual SD Card" and "Clear All Content & Settings" options — both must be checked; turn off "Find Device" before signing out of Xiaomi account.
OPPO / OnePlus Settings > Additional Settings > Restore Phone > Completely Clear All Data ColorOS provides a "thorough clear" mode that overwrites storage multiple times; requires lock screen password confirmation.
vivo Settings > System Management > Backup & Reset > Clear All Data Must check "Format Phone Storage" to clean the SD card area; must sign out of vivo account and turn off "Find Phone."
Samsung Settings > General Management > Reset > Factory Reset Must remove Samsung account and turn off "Find My Mobile" first; some models have an "auto-overwrite" option, recommended to enable.
3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things Separately Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone > Erase All Content and Settings Must sign out of Apple ID first, otherwise the next user will be blocked by iCloud Activation Lock; iOS 15+ supports "Keep iCloud Data When Signing Out" for later reference.

The Three Most Overlooked Things

  • Not Signing Out of Accounts: Phone gets remotely locked after selling to the next buyer, and you can't get back in either — ultimately you have to take your ID to an official service center to unlock it.
  • SD Card Not Removed: Factory reset doesn't format photos on the external SD card — remember to manually remove or separately format it.
  • USB Drive / OTG Peripheral Not Disconnected: If peripherals are connected during the wipe, it may accidentally clear their data or cause the wipe to be interrupted.

Manual backup

The data in your phone is no longer "virtual." It carries your money, social relationships, creative works, and even your "digital identity."After a person passes away, how should these assets be handled?This is no longer an abstract question — it's a real dilemma facing more and more families: relatives don't know the passwords, platforms won't allow inheritance, and cryptocurrency is lost forever.

Legal Basis: Article 49 of the Personal Information Protection Law

Article 49 of the Personal Information Protection Law of the People's Republic of China, effective in 2021, clearly states:When a natural person dies, their close relatives may, for their own legitimate and proper interests, exercise the rights to access, copy, correct, and delete the deceased's personal information as provided in this Chapter, unless the deceased made other arrangements during their lifetime.

This means:

  • Close relatives have a legal basisto request platforms to process the deceased's accounts and personal information.
  • "Legitimate and proper interests" typically include handling inheritance, closing accounts, and deleting sensitive privacy information.
  • If the deceased made other arrangements during their lifetime (such as designating a legacy contact), those arrangements take precedence.
  • Platforms cannot use "user privacy" as a blanket reason to refuse cooperation, but specific procedures vary by platform.
1. WeChat and Alipay: Accounts Can't Be Inherited, But Funds Can

The rules for these two most commonly used apps among Chinese people are different:

  • WeChat Account: According to the Tencent WeChat Software License and Service Agreement, account ownership belongs to Tencent — users only have usage rights,the account itself cannot be inherited or transferred. However, theWallet balance and Qian fundsare personal property. Close relatives can apply to Tenpay for withdrawal or transfer with a death certificate, proof of kinship, and an inheritance notarization.
  • Alipay: The account also cannot be directly inherited, but Alipay balance, Yuebao, and wealth management fundsare inheritable property. Heirs can handle this through Alipay's customer service hotline or by submitting a death certificate and inheritance notarization offline; Ant Wealth financial products require going through the fund company's process.
  • Chat History: Legally classified as personal privacy — platforms won't proactively provide it to family members. If it involves inheritance leads, it can be obtained through litigation or notarization application.

Enable "screen sharing" or "remote control" for strangers.

  • Don't directly hand the deceased's account passwords to family members to "keep using"— this violates platform agreements, and it's harder to prove things if funds are frozen or risk control is triggered.
  • Don't try to use the deceased's phone to receive verification codes for "withdrawals"— this may be classified as theft and could violate the law.
  • Don't Delay: Some accounts are automatically deactivated after long periods of inactivity, making fund recovery more difficult.
2. Apple's "Legacy Contact": Designate in Advance for Half the Effort, Double the Result

Starting from iOS 15.2, Apple launched the "Legacy Contact" feature, allowing users to designate trusted contacts in advance. After the user's passing, the contact can usedeath certificate + Legacy Contact access keyto request access to the deceased's iCloud data (photos, notes, contacts, etc.). Steps:

  1. On iPhone, go to [Settings] > [Your Name] > [Sign-In & Security] > [Legacy Contact]Trivia: What is README
  2. Tap "Add Legacy Contact" and confirm identity with Face ID.
  3. Select a contact (from your contacts), and the system will generate anAccess KeyTrivia: What is README
  4. Send the access key to the other person via SMS, email, or printed copy, and remind them to keep it safe.
  5. Multiple contacts can be added as backup to avoid single-point failure.

The designated person doesn't need an Apple device — they can request access on Apple's official website with the key and death certificate. The entire process typically completes within 7 days.

3. Google's "Inactive Account Manager": Automatically Handling Digital Aftermath

Google provides the "Inactive Account Manager," which can automatically execute preset actions when the user hasn't logged in for a long time — this is one of the most comprehensive digital legacy mechanisms available.

  1. ). myaccount.google.com/inactive, sign in to your Google account.
  2. Set the timeout period: triggers after 3 / 6 / 12 / 18 months of inactivity.
  3. Add trusted contacts (up to 10), and set which data each can access (Gmail, Photos, Drive, etc.).
  4. Optional: Set up auto-reply email to inform senders you can no longer respond.
  5. Final choice: when the timeout expires, eitherShare data with contacts, orDelete the accountTrivia: What is README
  6. Set a phone number as fallback verification to prevent accidental triggering.
4. Domestic Social Media Accounts: Memorialization and Deletion Process

Domestic mainstream social platforms handle deceased users' accounts in two ways:"Memorialization" (preserving the account for remembrance)verb"Deletion" (complete removal). Family members can apply to platform customer service with a death certificate, proof of kinship, and the applicant's ID.

  • Weibo: Supports account "memorialization." Relatives apply with a death certificate — the account is locked and can't be logged into, but content is preserved. The profile page displays "This account has been set as a memorial account." Deletion can also be requested, requiring an inheritance notarization.
  • Douyin: Through "Me - Settings - Feedback & Help - Account & Security - Account Deletion" or manual customer service, submit a death certificate, proof of kinship, and applicant ID. After review, the account can be deleted or converted to memorial status.
  • Bilibili: Submit the deceased's certificate and proof of kinship through customer service channels. You can request account deletion or preservation as a memorial page; handling of the uploader's historical content requires consideration of copyright declarations.
  • Xiaohongshu (RED): Appeal through official customer service, submit death certificate and proof of kinship, can request account deletion and content removal.

Key Reminders

  • Platform rules may be updated — check the latest official customer service guidelines before proceeding.
  • All certification documents should be scanned and backed up before submission. Keep originals safe.
  • When handling multiple platforms at once, you can apply for a singleinheritance notarizationto save repeated trips.
5. The Challenge of Digital Asset Inheritance

In addition to social accounts, more and more people holdgenuinely valuable digital assets, whose inheritance issues are more complex:

  • Cryptocurrency (Bitcoin, Ethereum, etc.): Based on the principle of "private key = ownership,"no private key means the assets are gone. Heirs can't appeal "on-chain" through legal documents. Recommendation: store mnemonics/private keys in shards across multiple physical security locations (such as a bank safe deposit box + home safe), and specify the access method in your will.
  • Exchange Accounts: Similar to bank accounts, can apply to exchanges (such as Binance, OKX) for asset disposition with an inheritance notarization, but cross-border exchange processes are lengthy.
  • Domain Names: Inheritable property. Heirs can transfer ownership at the domain registrar (such as Alibaba Cloud, GoDaddy) after submitting an inheritance notarization.
  • Intellectual Property (original articles, videos, patents, software copyrights): Property rights within copyright can be inherited (personal rights are not inherited), and revenue rights can be enjoyed by heirs until 50 years after the author's death.
  • Cloud Storage and Network Drives: Content data belongs to the individual and can be inherited; however, some platform agreements stipulate that accounts themselves are non-transferable — you need to download data first before deletion.

The Real Cost of Cryptocurrency "Disappearance"

According to Chainalysis reports, globallyover 3 million Bitcoinshave been permanently lost due to lost private keys — equivalent to one-sixth of the existing total. If you hold crypto assets, be sure to let at least one person you absolutely trust know therecovery path— otherwise these assets will sleep forever on the blockchain.

6. A "Digital Will" Template

Traditional property wills can't manage digital assets. I recommend updating a "digital will" addendum annually, stored alongside your official will. The following template is for reference:

"Personal Digital Asset Disposition Addendum" (Template)

Part One: Account Inventory(Record only account names and platforms — do NOT write passwords）

  • Social: WeChat (account xxx), Weibo, Douyin, Bilibili, Xiaohongshu, etc.
  • Payment: Alipay, WeChat Pay, various bank card apps
  • Cloud: iCloud, Huawei Cloud, Mi Cloud, Google account, Microsoft account
  • Email: QQ Mail, NetEase Mail, Gmail, etc.
  • Other: Cloud drives, subscription services, game accounts, etc.

Part Two: Password Custody Plan

  • Master password storage: Use a password manager (like Bitwarden, 1Password). Write the master password on paper and seal it in a home safe.
  • Recovery keys/mnemonics: Store in fragments across at least two physical locations (e.g., bank safe deposit box + home safe).
  • Authorized contact: Name, ID number, relationship, contact information.

Part Three: Disposition Wishes

  • Whether each type of account should be "memorialized" or "deactivated."
  • Whether iCloud / Google data has a designated "Legacy Contact" or "Inactive Account Manager."
  • Who inherits crypto assets, with instructions for private key access.
  • Who enjoys the proceeds from copyrighted works.

Part Four: Contacts and Platforms

  • Trusted executor: name, contact, backup contact.
  • Platform customer service contacts and required documentation checklist.
  • This addendum updated: ____/__/__. Next review date: ____/__/__.

Legal Note on "Passwords"

Writing passwords directly into a will poses leak risks, and all heirs can see them once the will is probated.A safer approach: the will only contains "account inventory + disposition wishes + password custody location." Actual passwords are transmitted separately to the trusted executor via the password manager's master password. This satisfies legal requirements while reducing password leak risks.

Give it a second life

A single phone contains dozens of metals including gold, silver, copper, and rare earth elements. Discarding it carelessly pollutes soil and wastes resources. There are three proper recycling channels, each with different strengths:

  • : Convert it into a car navigator, smart home hub, or surveillance camera.: Most recommended — standardized process, data security guaranteed. Apple, Huawei, Xiaomi, and other brands have "trade-in" entries on their official websites. After assessment, the value can be deducted from the new phone price.
  • Last backup and log out of all accounts.: Choose a reputable large recycling platform. After placing an order, SF Express picks up the device, and payment is made after inspection. Be sure to choose aplatform that provides a "data wiping report", and keep the receipt.
  • Charitable Donation: Contact local rural schools or community organizations — old phones can be converted into educational tablets or phones for the elderly.Before donating, be sure to perform a complete wipe and remove all SIM/SD cardsTrivia: What is README
  • (Optional) Fill storage with junk files, then factory reset again.: Repurpose as a car navigator, smart home controller, security camera, baby monitor, or digital photo frame. An old phone can serve for several more years.

The Truth About E-Waste

A phone's circuit board containsgold, silver, palladium, copperand other precious metals. Per ton of scrap circuit boards contains tens of times more gold than gold ore. But if discarded carelessly, the lead, mercury, and cadmium will leach into soil and groundwater, polluting for decades.Proper recycling protects the environment and allows scarce metals to be recycled.

Chapter 26: Current Smartphone Technology Frontier

Having covered old phones' "afterlife," let's look at the present. 2024-2026 is a concentrated explosion period for phone technology: AI moved from cloud to pocket, satellite communication trickled down from flagships to mid-range, foldable screens went from "novelty" to "daily use," and battery technology saw material-level breakthroughs not seen in years. This chapter surveys these cutting-edge technologies to help you decide "should I upgrade now" and "what to upgrade to."

I. AI Phones: Marketing Gimmick or Real Revolution?

Since 2024, nearly all Android manufacturers have branded their flagships as "AI phones," and Apple launched Apple Intelligence in iOS 18. But what truly qualifies as an "AI phone"? The industry has roughly converged on three criteria:

  • On-device LLMs: The phone can run a language model with around 7B parameters locally (like lightweight versions of Qwen, Llama, DeepSeek), completing text summarization, translation, and copywriting without cloud dependency. Test: if AI features still work in Airplane Mode, it's an on-device model.
  • NPU Computing Power (TOPS): NPU (Neural Processing Unit) computing power is measured in TOPS (trillions of operations per second). 2024 flagship chips (like Snapdragon 8 Gen3, Dimensity 9300) have 40-70 TOPS; 2025-2026 new-generation chips generally exceed 100 TOPS — the hardware threshold for running LLMs on-device.
  • AI Agent Scenarios: Not just "Q&A" — can execute cross-app task chains. For example, "organize yesterday's meeting photos into an album and share with Zhang San" — the system automatically calls Photos, Files, WeChat, and other apps to complete the task. This is the core differentiator between an AI phone and a "phone with an AI assistant."

II. Manufacturer AI Strategy Comparison: Who's Serious, Who's Labeling?

Each manufacturer's AI route differs significantly — worth paying attention to when purchasing:

  • Apple Apple Intelligence (iOS 18+): Emphasizes system-level app integration — email summaries, notification priority, writing polish, AI photo editing. Primarily on-device models, with complex tasks offloaded to Private Cloud Compute. Advantages: privacy protection and system smoothness. Disadvantages: slower Chinese language rollout, with some features only gradually supported in 2025.
  • Google Gemini Nano: Built into Pixel 8/9 series, supports "Circle to Search," Magic Compose, recording summaries, etc. Gemini Nano is a true on-device small model, open-source ecosystem friendly, and the reference implementation for Android AI phones.
  • : Real-time call translation, note AI summaries, image generation and editing, search circle selection, and other functions.: Integrates HarmonyOS Xiaoyi, supporting on-device copywriting, AI photo editing, AI eraser (removing passersby), and call summaries. After HarmonyOS NEXT 5.0, further system-level integration deeply fuses AI capabilities with the OS.
  • Xiaomi MiLM (Mi Large Model): Built into HyperOS, supports AI portraits, AI summaries, AI artist, super resolution. Xiaomi follows an "on-device + cloud collaboration" route — lightweight models run on-device, heavy tasks go to cloud.
  • OPPO (Andes Large Model) and vivo (Blue Heart Large Model): Deeply integrated into ColorOS 15 and OriginOS 5, focusing on AI eraser, AI document summaries, AI image Q&A, and natural language photo search ("find photos I took at the beach last year").

Buying Advice: If you frequently need AI for work documents and information organization, prioritize models with strong on-device computing and system-level AI integration. If you only occasionally use AI for photo editing, mainstream mid-range phones are sufficient.

III. Satellite Communication: From Flagship "Gimmick" to Mid-Range Standard

Satellite communication is one of the most substantial technology trickle-downs in recent years. When Huawei Mate 60 and iPhone 14 debuted it in 2022, it was flagship-exclusive; by 2025, it has reached the 2,000-3,000 yuan tier.

  • BeiDou Short Messages Reach Mid-Range: BeiDou satellite short message functionality (sending texts up to 1,000 Chinese characters + location) has reached mid-range models from Redmi, realme, iQOO, etc. No monthly fee, free to use. Suitable for hiking, road trips, and similar scenarios.
  • Tiantong Satellite Calls: Huawei Mate 60/70 series, Honor Magic6 series, etc. support Tiantong-1 satellite calling — can make/receive satellite calls and send satellite messages. Requires a carrier satellite plan (about 10-200 yuan/month), suitable for users who frequently enter remote areas.
  • iPhone Satellite Messages (SOS): iPhone 14 and later support satellite SOS — can send text messages to emergency services and share location. Free for 2 years, renewable in some regions.
  • Explore: Your Phone's Video Settings: Urban users basically don't need it, but outdoor enthusiasts and business travelers to remote areas should strongly consider satellite-capable models — it can save lives at critical moments.

IV. Foldable Screen Ecosystem Maturity: Ready to Be a Primary Phone?

Foldable screens have gone from "tech novelty" to "viable primary phone." To judge foldable maturity, look at three things: hardware durability, app adaptation, and interaction ecosystem.

  • Hardware Durability: Hinge life generally exceeds 500,000 folds (100 folds/day for 13 years), water-drop hinges reduce screen creases, IPX8 water resistance is now standard. UTG glass + screen protector makes the inner screen less "delicate."
  • App Adaptation: Mainstream apps (WeChat, Taobao, Douyin, Bilibili, Office, WPS) are adapted for large screens, but about 30% of long-tail apps remain unadapted, showing stretched or letterboxed. Try your frequently used apps before purchasing.
  • Flex Mode Interaction: When folded to 90°-120°, some apps support a flex mode with "top screen for content, bottom screen for controls," suitable for video calls, selfies, and watching videos. Flex-mode selfies are a foldable-exclusive experience.
  • Split Screen and Multitasking: On the large screen, you can run two apps in split screen, or even three apps in floating windows. HyperOS, ColorOS, and OriginOS split-screen logic is fairly mature, but iOS (iPadOS-style) split screen isn't available on iPhone.
  • Price: Horizontal folds (book-style) dropped from 10,000+ yuan to 5,000-7,000 yuan tier; vertical folds (flip-style) dropped to 4,000-5,000 yuan. In 2025, some manufacturers launched 3,000-yuan vertical folds — foldables truly entered the mass market.

Buying Advice: If you're a heavy reader, document processor, or video consumer, horizontal foldables are worth considering. If you prioritize portability and social appeal, vertical foldables are more suitable. Spend at least 30 minutes trying one in-store before deciding.

V. 6G and Wi-Fi 7: Speed and Boundaries of Next-Gen Connectivity

While 6G hasn't truly landed, related technologies are already on the way:

  • 6G Progress: 3GPP plans to complete 6G standardization by 2027, with commercial deployment around 2030. 6G theoretical peak rates can reach 1 Tbps (50x of 5G), latency as low as 0.1ms, supporting "integrated sensing and communication" — phones could even serve as low-precision radar. Currently, manufacturers are still in prototype verification, far from consumer products.
  • Wi-Fi 7（802.11be）: Became flagship standard from 2024, with theoretical peak rates of 46 Gbps (4x Wi-Fi 6), supporting 320MHz bandwidth, 4K-QAM, and MLO (Multi-Link Operation). Real-world testing shows 2-5 Gbps transfer rates on flagships with Wi-Fi 7 routers, 2-3x faster than Wi-Fi 6E. If you get a Wi-Fi 7 phone, remember to pair it with a Wi-Fi 7 router to unlock full performance.
  • Bluetooth 5.4 and LE Audio: 2024-2026 phones widely support Bluetooth 5.4 and LE Audio (Low Energy Audio) — can connect two headphone pairs simultaneously to listen to the same song, and Auracast broadcast audio lets multiple people sync to the same audio source in public spaces.

VI. Silicon-Carbon Anode Batteries: Battery Life Finally Gets a Material-Level Breakthrough

Phone battery life has long been criticized as "one charge per day." Since 2024, the adoption of silicon-carbon anode battery technology has brought substantial improvement.

  • Technical Principle: Traditional graphite anodes have a theoretical capacity of about 372 mAh/g. Silicon's theoretical capacity is as high as 4200 mAh/g (~10x), but silicon expands 300% during charge/discharge, causing pulverization. Silicon-carbon anodes use a nano-silicon-carbon composite structure to control silicon expansion within acceptable limits, boosting energy density by 15%-30%.
  • Actual performance: 2024-2025 flagships with silicon-carbon anodes (like Xiaomi 14 Ultra, Honor Magic 6 Ultimate, vivo X100 Pro, etc.) fit 5000-6000 mAh batteries in 7-8mm bodies — about 800-1000 mAh more than the previous generation. Heavy use can last a day and a half.
  • 100W+ Fast Charging Compatibility: Silicon-carbon anodes have good fast-charging compatibility — 100W/120W fully charging in 17 minutes is no longer news. In 2025, some models support 150W-240W, reaching 80% in 10 minutes.
  • Buying Advice: If you're a heavy user, prioritize post-2024 models with the "silicon-carbon anode + 100W+ fast charging" combo — battery anxiety will be greatly reduced.

  • Satellite communication: BeiDou short messages reach mid-range, Tiantong calls still flagship-only.
  • Foldable screens: hardware mature, 70% app adaptation, flex mode/split screen are unique experiences.
  • 6G is still on the way, Wi-Fi 7 has landed, Bluetooth LE Audio is spreading.
  • Silicon-carbon anode + 100W+ fast charging: dual breakthrough in battery life and charging.

Take a piece of paper and list your needs for AI, satellite, foldable screens, Wi-Fi 7, fast charging, and battery capacity in three tiers: "Must-have / Nice-to-have / Don't need." This way, next time you visit a store, you can quickly judge whether the salesperson's "selling points" are real needs or just upselling. For example:

  • Nice-to-have: on-device AI summaries, Wi-Fi 7, BeiDou short messages.
  • Don't need: foldable screen (I prefer bar phones), satellite calls (I don't travel far), 240W extreme fast charging.

Chapter 27: Making Phones Easy for Parents — Complete Senior-Friendly Guide

Honestly, when writing this chapter, I thought of my own parents. Every time a "system update" pops up on my mom's phone, she's afraid to tap it, worried she'll break the phone. My dad's WeChat font is smaller than an ant, but he doesn't know how to enlarge it — he's been squinting at it for two years. It's not that they're "dumb" — it's that phones default to assuming everyone is a twenty-something. In this chapter, I use the plainest language to solve the most frustrating problems elderly users face with their phones, one by one.

0. First, Get the Mindset Right: It's Not "Seniors Can't Use Phones" — It's "Phones Weren't Designed for Them"

Before making any settings changes, one concept needs to be clear:Current smartphone interfaces were never really designed with elderly users in mind. Pop-ups are too small to see, gestures require precise touches, icons all look the same — these aren't user problems, they're product problems. So when helping elderly relatives with phones, the first thing isn't to teach — it's to help themset up the environment. Once the environment is set up properly, most problems disappear.

Three iron rules for helping elderly relatives with phones: ① Don't rush— you've used smartphones for ten years, they may have used them for three months. ② Use analogies— "Wi-Fi is like the water pipes at home — turn on the faucet and water flows." This kind of metaphor is infinitely easier to understand than technical jargon. ③ Write it down— they might forget verbal instructions. Write the key steps on a piece of paper and stick it to the back of their phone case — it works better than anything else.

I. First Step: Enable "Easy Mode" — The Phone Becomes Clean and Simple

Most phones now have a built-in "Easy Mode" (some call it "Care Mode," "Senior Mode," or "Elder Mode"). After enabling it, the entire phone transforms:

  • Fonts and icons become very large— no more need for reading glasses to see the screen.
  • Desktop icons greatly simplified— only Phone, Messages, Camera, Photos, WeChat, and a few other commonly used apps remain; everything else is tucked away.
  • Operations become simpler— many flashy features (leftmost page, smart assistant, floating windows, etc.) are disabled by default — the interface is clean and straightforward.
  • Sound becomes louder— ringtone, notification, and call volumes are automatically set to maximum.
How to enable Easy Mode by brand (just follow along):
Brand Mode Name How to Enable
3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things SeparatelyAccessibility (no separate Easy Mode, but items can be enlarged individually)Settings > Display & Brightness > Text Size, drag to max. Then go to "Accessibility > Display & Text Size" and enable "Bold Text" and "Button Shapes"
4. Wireless Charging ProtocolsEasy ModeSettings > System & Updates > Easy Mode > Enable

If you use another brand, search for "简易" (easy) or "长辈" (elder) in the search box at the top of Settings — you'll usually find it. If not, follow the "Manual Enlargement" approach below step by step — the result is the same.

II. If You Don't Use Easy Mode, Manual Adjustment Works Too — "Big Text + Big Icons" in Five Steps

Some elderly relatives don't want to use Easy Mode — they think it looks too "old-fashioned." In that case, manually adjust these five items for the same effect:

  1. Set Font to Maximum: Settings > Display > Font Size, drag to the far right. Also set "Display Size" (sometimes called "Display Zoom") to maximum — this makes all interface elements larger together.
  2. Make Icons Bigger: Pinch on the home screen (like zooming out on a photo) to enter desktop settings > Desktop Layout (or Icon Size), and choose the layout with the fewest grid cells (like 3×5) — icons naturally become bigger.
  3. Enable "High Contrast Text": Makes text edges sharper — find this toggle in "Accessibility."
  4. Disable Unnecessary Notifications: Settings > Notifications, turn off all app notifications except Phone, Messages, and WeChat. This way the phone won't buzz every few minutes and won't feel annoying.
  5. Put Frequently Contacted People on the Home Screen: Long-press empty space on home screen > Add Widget > Contacts, and place speed-dial shortcuts for spouse, children, doctor, and emergency contacts on the home screen. One tap to call — no need to scroll through contacts.

Hands-On: Help Elderly Relatives "Renovate" Their Phone

  1. Enable Easy Mode (follow the brand table above).
  2. Turn on battery percentage display (Settings > Battery > Battery Percentage), so they always know how much charge is left.
  3. Open the notification shade and remove or hide quick toggles like Bluetooth, NFC, and Airplane Mode that elderly relatives don't need.
  4. Place four speed-dial contacts on the home screen: spouse, children, family doctor (if any), community/property management.

III. Anti-Fraud — Please Read This Section Together with Your Elderly Relatives

Elderly people are prime targets for telecom fraud. It's not that they're less vigilant — scammers' scripts are carefully designed to exploit elderly people's psychological vulnerabilities. Here are the most common scam types and how to respond. I recommend reading them aloud to your elderly relatives, or printing them out and sticking them next to the phone.

Six Common Scams (Hang Up Immediately If You Encounter These):
  • ① "Your Grandson Is in Trouble, Send Money Now"— The scammer says "your grandson/granddaughter got into trouble outside, was arrested by police, and needs bail." Remember:Any call demanding a transfer to "release someone" is a scam. Police and government agencies never demand money over the phone.
  • ② "Your Health Insurance Card Has Been Suspended"— A text message says your health insurance card is abnormal and asks you to click a link to "activate" it. Remember:Health insurance and social security bureaus never send text messages asking you to click links. In this situation, call 12333 (the official social security hotline) to verify.
  • ③ "High-Yield Investment, Guaranteed Profit"— WeChat groups and text messages recommend various "retirement investments" and "government-supported projects," promising high returns. Remember:Anything promising annualized returns over 5% that's "guaranteed" is 99.9% a scamTrivia: What is README
  • ④ "I'm Your Boss/Old Friend, I Changed My Number"— Impersonating an acquaintance to borrow money. Remember:Calling to verify works better than anything. If they say "I can't take calls," they're almost certainly a scammer.
  • ⑤ "Free Eggs / Health Product Seminar"— Free offline events lure elderly people into attending "health seminars" and then sell overpriced health products. Remember:There's no free lunch — free events are always businesses in disguiseTrivia: What is README
  • ⑥ "Your Phone Is Infected, Needs Remote Repair"— The scammer asks you to download a remote control app (like Sunflower, TeamViewer), then remotely controls your phone to transfer money. Remember:Absolutely never let anyone remotely control your phone!Phone manufacturers, carriers, and banks will never call you asking you to install remote control software.
Three defense lines that, once set up, can block 90% of scams:
  1. First Line: Built-in Phone Blocking— On Android, enable "Harassment Blocking" (in the Phone app or Phone Manager app). On iPhone, enable "Silence Unknown Callers" (Settings > Phone > Silence Unknown Callers).
  2. Second Line: Carrier Blocking— Send text "KTFSR" to 10086 to activate China Mobile's free high-frequency spam call blocking. China Telecom and China Unicom have similar services. Call your carrier's customer service to have them enable it for you.
  3. Third Line: National Anti-Fraud Center App— Download the "National Anti-Fraud Center" app from the app store, register, and enable incoming call alerts. This app is linked to police databases — scam numbers are identified as soon as they call.

Anti-Fraud Mantra for Elderly Relatives (Print and Stick Next to the Phone)

  • ☎ Stranger calls asking for money transfer → Hang up!
  • 🔗 Text message links asking you to click → Delete!
  • 💰 Promising high returns with guaranteed principal → Block!
  • 📱 Asking you to install remote control software → Hang up immediately!
  • 👮 Real police don't handle cases over the phone, and definitely don't ask for money!
  • ❤ When unsure about anything, call your children first.

IV. Remote Assistance — Fix Your Parents' Phone from Anywhere

Sometimes elderly relatives encounter problems that you can't explain over the phone — they can't find the right button. That's when "remote assistance" comes in — you can see their phone screen on your own phone and help them operate it. Each brand has a different solution:

  • 4. Wireless Charging Protocols: Built-in "Changlian" app has a "Screen Sharing" feature. Both you and your parents install Changlian, start a video call, and tap "Share Screen" — you can draw circles on their screen to point out "tap here."
  • Xiaomi/Redmi: Xiaomi Video Call app has "Remote Assistance," supporting screen sharing + simultaneous voice call.
  • [Install Apps from External Sources]: Built-in "Family Space" or "Remote Guardian" — search for "远程" (remote) in Settings to find it.
  • Universal Solution (Works for All Brands): Download the "Sunflower Remote Control" app (free version is sufficient). Install it on both phones. Register the same account or add as friends. Have your parents read you the verification code displayed on their phone, and you can remotely view and operate their screen.
  • : If you need to extract text from scanned documents for editing, you need OCR. WeChat's built-in "Extract Text" feature is the simplest — long-press the image to use it, and the recognition accuracy is decent. For bulk processing, you can use the Baimiao app or CamScanner. For Chinese recognition, Baidu's OCR engine works quite well; WPS's image-to-text feature is also very accurate.: FaceTime supports "Screen Sharing" during calls. While on a FaceTime call, tap the screen share button, and the other person can see your screen. But iOS security prevents remote operation — it's "instructive teaching" only.

V. WeChat "Senior-Friendly Makeover" — Just Tell Your Parents These Things

WeChat is the app elderly people use most, but the interface is too dense and cluttered. Here are some quick, effective adjustments:

  • Enlarge WeChat's Own Font: WeChat > Me > Settings > General > Font Size, drag to maximum. Note: this only affects the font within WeChat, not the system font.
  • Enable "Care Mode": WeChat > Me > Settings > Care Mode > Enable. After enabling, fonts and buttons become larger, color contrast is enhanced, and you can one-tap "Listen to Text Messages" (tap a text message and it reads aloud).
  • Help Them Label Important Contacts: Change children's and relatives' names in contacts to easily recognizable ones — like "Eldest Son - Xiaoming" or "Second Daughter - Xiaohong," so they immediately know who's who when opening WeChat.
  • Teach Them to Use "Voice Input" Instead of Typing: On the keyboard next to the chat box, hold the spacebar (Android) or tap the microphone icon (iPhone), and speak directly — it converts to text and sends. Recognition accuracy is already very high — for elderly people who can't type in pinyin, it's a "game-changing" convenience.
  • Disable Unused Features in "Discover": WeChat > Me > Settings > General > Discover Page Management, turn off "Moments," "Channels," "Live," "Shopping," "Games" — anything not used — to reduce clutter.

VI. What If the Phone Is Lost? Make an "Emergency Plan" for Elderly Relatives

Preparation prevents problems. While the phone isn't lost yet, do these things first:

  1. Confirm "Find My Phone" Is Enabled: iPhone — Settings > [Your Name] > Find My > Find My iPhone; Android — search for "Find Device" in Settings. Make sure this toggle is on.
  2. Write Important Passwords and Accounts on a Piece of Paper: Lock one copy of Apple ID / Huawei account / Xiaomi account passwords in a home drawer, and give another copy to a trusted child. If the phone is lost, you need these accounts to remotely lock and locate it — forgetting the password makes it very difficult.
  3. Teach Elderly Relatives One Sentence(Background)."If the phone is lost, the first thing to do is call family."Family can immediately log into iCloud or Android's Find My Device website to remotely mark it as "Lost Mode" — the person who finds it can't unlock or use it.

VII. Wireless Earphones and Hearing Aid Compatibility — An Overlooked Feature

Many elderly relatives have hearing issues but don't know that phones can work with hearing aids. iPhone and some Android phones support MFi (Made for iPhone) hearing aids, which can directly transmit phone call audio to the hearing aid — much clearer than holding the phone to the ear.

  • Connection Method: iPhone Settings > Accessibility > Hearing Devices, turn on Bluetooth, and follow the hearing aid's pairing instructions.
  • If Not Using a Hearing Aid: In "Accessibility > Audio/Visual," enable "Phone Noise Cancellation" and "Mono Audio" to improve call clarity.
  • iOS: In "Accessibility > Hearing Enhancement," there are similar settings — locations vary by brand. Search for "助听" (hearing aid) directly.

VIII. Health-Related Features — A Phone Is More Than a Communication Tool

  • SOS Emergency: Press the power button five times consecutively (on most phones), and the phone automatically calls emergency services and sends location to preset emergency contacts. Set this up for elderly relatives in advance — iPhone: "Settings > Emergency SOS"; Android: "Settings > Safety > Emergency Assistance." Practice once before teaching them, so they don't fumble when stressed.
  • Fall Detection: Apple Watch has this feature — if it detects a fall followed by no movement, it automatically calls emergency services and notifies family. If budget allows, getting one for elderly relatives can save lives at critical moments.
  • Medication Reminders: iPhone's "Health" app has a built-in medication reminder — set the medication name, time, and dosage, and it pops up a reminder when it's time. Android can use "alarm clocks" or download "medication reminder" apps.

Chapter Summary

  • Enable Easy Mode or manually enlarge fonts/icons first — once the environment is set up, most problems disappear
  • Three iron rules for helping elderly relatives with phones: don't rush, use analogies, write it down
  • Remind about six common scams repeatedly — three defense lines can block 90% of fraud
  • Remote assistance lets you fix your parents' phone from anywhere
  • WeChat's "Care Mode" + "Voice Input" are the two most practical features for elderly users
  • SOS Emergency and Fall Detection — life-saving configurations worth spending five minutes to set up

Chapter 28: Spend Wisely on Your Dream Phone — The Ultimate Smartphone Buying Guide

When buying a phone, many people spend a week reading reviews, a month comparing prices, then end up spending five or six thousand on a flagship they don't actually need. This chapter doesn't list spec sheets — you can find those on official websites. What I want to give you is a "phone selection mindset" — so no matter what new phone hits the market, you can judge whether it suits you.

0. Three-Step Phone Selection: Needs → Budget → Model

Many people ask online "what phone should I buy for 3,000 yuan?" — this question can't actually be answered, because we don't know what you'll primarily use the phone for. The correct thinking order when buying a phone should be:

Three-Step Phone Selection

  1. First, figure out what you care about most: Photography? Gaming? Battery life? Screen? System smoothness? Or just need to make calls and use WeChat? Prioritize your needs.
  2. Then, Set a Budget Ceiling: Not "roughly how much" but "the maximum I'm willing to spend." Set a hard ceiling so you don't keep looking at pricier options.
  3. Finally, Pick a Model: Use your prioritized needs and budget to match with models.

I. How to Read Core Specs — You Don't Need to Understand Everything, Just These Five

Spec sheets have dozens of data points, but ordinary users only need to focus on these five dimensions:

Dimension How to Evaluate One-Sentence Summary
Processor (SoC) Determines how many years the phone will stay smooth. 2026 standards: Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen5 / Dimensity 9500 and above = top tier; Snapdragon 8s Gen4 / Dimensity 8400 = mid-to-high; Snapdragon 7+ Gen4 / Dimensity 7350 = good for three years. Below Snapdragon 6-series — be cautious. Buy new, not old — SoC determines how many years your phone stays lag-free
Screen OLED has better colors and is more power-efficient than LCD; 120Hz refresh rate is noticeably smoother than 60Hz; resolution should be at least 1080P. High-frequency PWM dimming (1920Hz+) is more eye-friendly. OLED + 120Hz + high-frequency dimming = the baseline for a good screen
Using Huawei phone → prioritize HarmonyOS Connect, best experience with Huawei devices. Don't Look at Megapixels — Look at Sensor Size. Sensor size matters much more than megapixels. Ultrawide is practical; telephoto (3x+ optical zoom) for distant subjects; macro lenses are mostly filler. Large-sensor main camera + practical telephoto > multiple filler lenses
Battery and Charging 4500mAh is the baseline; 5000mAh+ easily lasts a day. For fast charging: 60W+ is fast, 100W+ is blazing fast. Wireless charging is convenient but slow. 5000mAh + 60W fast charging = anxiety-free combo
System Update Commitment Determines how long the phone stays secure. Apple typically provides 5-6 years of system updates; Samsung flagships get 4 years system + 5 years security updates; Google Pixel gets 7 years; domestic mid-range phones generally have shorter commitments (2-3 years). Want to use it longer — choose a brand with long update commitments

III. Choose by Scenario — What Are Your Needs?

Here are the most common "user profiles" — just find the one that matches you:

4. "Ears" for Hearing-Impaired Users—Complete Live Captions Guide Key Specs to Look For Recommended Direction
📸 Photography Enthusiast Large-sensor main camera (1-inch ideal), OIS, telephoto (3x+ optical zoom), imaging chip vivo X series, Huawei Pura/Mate series, Xiaomi Ultra series
🎮 Gamer Top-tier processor, high touch sampling rate, cooling system, large battery + fast charging iQOO Digital series, ROG Phone, RedMagic, Redmi K series

🌍 International Travel eSIM support, complete global band coverage, Google services iPhone, Samsung S series, Pixel, OnePlus

IV. Five Common Pitfalls — Check Before You Buy

  1. Pitfall 1: Four or Five Cameras Don't Equal Good Photos— Manufacturers love to stack lens numbers in specs, but two of them are often 2MP "filler lenses" (macro + depth) that are practically useless. When evaluating a phone's photography, only look at the main + ultrawide + telephoto— these three are enough. You can pretend the rest don't exist.
  2. Pitfall 2: Don't Be Fooled by 108 Megapixels— High megapixel count doesn't mean good image quality. Sensor size, aperture, and algorithm tuning matter far more than pixel count. Many flagship phones use 50MP large-sensor cameras that produce photos far superior to some 108MP budget phones.
  3. Pitfall 3: Don't Buy Carrier-Locked Phones— "Deposit phone credit, get a free phone" looks like a great deal, but carrier-customized phones have slow system updates, non-removable pre-installed apps, and are usually carrier-locked (only work with that carrier's SIM card). You think you're saving money, but you're actually getting "locked in."
  4. Pitfall 4: "Curved Screens Are Premium" — Marketing, Not Truth— Curved screens were once a flagship signature, but more and more people are discovering their problems: hard to apply screen protectors, edge accidental touches, and expensive repairs when cracked. The 2026 trend is returning to "slightly curved" or even "completely flat" screens. Don't choose a curved screen just because "curved means premium."
  5. Pitfall 5: Not All "AI Phones" Are Actually Useful— In 2026, every manufacturer is shouting "AI phone," but many just renamed their existing voice assistant. Genuinely useful AI features include: real-time translation, AI eraser (removing people from photos), AI photo editing, on-device LLM inference, and localized smart summaries. Other flashy features are mostly gimmicks.

V. When Is the Best Time to Buy?

  • 618 Shopping Festival (late May to mid-June): The period with the biggest phone price drops of the year. Many manufacturers slash flagship prices by 800-1,500 yuan to boost sales. This is the best window for buying phones in the first half of the year.
  • Double 11 (late October to mid-November): The second-half mega sale, with discounts comparable to 618. Many brands release new flagships around this time, so the previous generation sees the biggest price drops.
  • One Month After New Release: At launch it's full price, but after a month, channel prices (third-party stores) typically drop by 200-500 yuan.
  • Two Weeks Before Chinese New Year to Lantern Festival: Brick-and-mortar stores clear inventory during the "New Year Goods Festival," and you can negotiate prices with staff.
  • Not Recommended Times: Buying on launch day — unless you really want to be among the first owners, launch prices are the most expensive.

VI. Where to Buy — Which Channels Are Reliable?

  • Brand Official Store / Tmall Flagship Store / JD.com Self-Operated: Safest option. No price advantage, but no worry about refurbished or counterfeit goods, and best after-sales service.
  • Pinduoduo "10 Billion Subsidy": Lowest prices, but only buy from stores labeled with "10 Billion Subsidy." Avoid unlabeled ones. Record an unboxing video when you receive the goods — you can return if there are issues.
  • Physical Retail Stores: You can touch and feel the phone. Note: Sales staff will push high-margin models (not the most suitable ones for you). Before visiting, lock in 2-3 target models online, and tell them "I only want to see these."
  • Used Platforms (Xianyu / Zhuanzhuan): Cheaper but risky. If buying used, remember three rules: require purchase invoice or order screenshot, require IMEI number for verification, only use platform transactions, never transfer money privatelyTrivia: What is README

Hands-On: Use This Method to Choose a Phone

  1. Take a piece of paper and write down your two core needs (e.g., battery life first, camera second).
  2. Set a budget ceiling (e.g., 3,500 yuan).
  3. Open JD.com or Tmall, filter by price, and circle 3-5 candidate models.
  4. Search Bilibili for "XX model one-month usage experience" (not first-day reviews, but genuine feelings after at least a month of use), and watch two or three videos.
  5. Confirm the channel is reliable before ordering, and record an unboxing video upon delivery.

Chapter Summary

  • Five core specs to check: processor, display, camera, battery/charging, system update commitment
  • 1,500-3,500 yuan is the best value-for-money sweet spot
  • Last year's flagship is a better deal than this year's mid-range
  • Five pitfalls: multi-camera scam, high-megapixel trap, carrier-customized phones, curved screen myth, AI gimmicks
  • 618 and Double 11 are the two best time windows for buying phones each year

Chapter 29: Digital Wellbeing — Building a Healthy Relationship with Your Phone

Have you ever experienced this: you only meant to scroll short videos for 5 minutes, then looked up and realized two hours had passed? Or lying in bed at night scrolling your phone, getting more and more awake, and finally falling asleep at 2 AM? Phones have changed our lives, but they're also quietly consuming our time and health. This chapter isn't about "quitting phones" — it's about helping you take back control.

I. Check Your "Screen Time" — Numbers Are a Wake-Up Call

Before making changes, understand the current situation. Your phone has a feature many people have never opened called "Screen Time" (iPhone) or "Digital Wellbeing" (Android). It tells you exactly how much time you spend on your phone each day and which apps that time goes to.

  • 3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things Separately: Settings > Screen Time > See All Activity. You'll see daily unlock counts, pickup counts, and time spent in each app.
  • iOS: Settings > Digital Wellbeing & Parental Controls. Huawei calls it "Healthy Phone Usage," Xiaomi calls it "Screen Time Management." Similar features, all showing daily usage data.

80% of people who see this data for the first time are shocked. A friend of mine discovered after checking that they spent over 4 hours a day on Douyin — that's 28 hours a week, equivalent to a part-time job. This kind of "digital shock" is the first step toward change.

II. Set App Time Limits — Install a Speed Limiter for Yourself

Once you know where the problem is, you can set targeted limits. No need to delete apps outright — just set a "daily allowance":

  1. 3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things Separately: Settings > Screen Time > App Limits > Add Limit. Select the app you want to restrict (e.g., Douyin) and set 30 minutes per day. When the time's up, the app icon grays out, and opening it requires an additional password entry.
  2. iOS: Settings > Digital Wellbeing > App Timers. Select an app and set a daily usage limit; when time's up, the app icon grays out.
  3. Tip: Set the limit password to something you don't use often and is hard to remember. If it's too easy to enter, you'll be tempted to "extend" every time, making the limit useless.

III. The Right Way to Use "Do Not Disturb" — Not Muting Notifications, But Muting Anxiety

Many people's phones buzz with notifications dozens of times a day, and each buzz interrupts their attention. You think you're just "glancing at a notification," but it actually takes 15-20 minutes to refocus after each interruption. Do Not Disturb isn't about "going offline" — it's about helping you regain control of your attention.

  • Schedule It: Set Do Not Disturb to automatically turn on from 10 PM to 7 AM. This way, your sleep won't be interrupted by a spam text message.
  • Allow Important Contacts Through: In Do Not Disturb settings, set "Allow Calls From" to "Favorites" or enable "Repeated Calls" (a second call within 3 minutes will ring normally). This way you won't miss emergency calls from family, but won't be bothered by sales calls.
  • Work Focus Mode: iPhone's "Focus" mode lets you set custom scenarios — for example, a "Work" focus only allows work-related app notifications, while a "Reading" focus silences all notifications.

IV. Eye Protection Relies on Habits, Not Apps — The 20-20-20 Rule

Prolonged screen time inevitably causes dry, sore eyes. Eye protection mode (blue light filter) helps somewhat, but what really works is changing your eye usage habits:

The 20-20-20 Rule

Every 20 minutes of screen time, look at something 20 feet (about 6 meters) away for 20 seconds. This simple action effectively relieves ciliary muscle fatigue.

  • Enable Eye Protection Mode: Settings > Display > Eye Protection (or Night Shift). When enabled, the screen's color temperature warms up, reducing blue light. Recommended to set it to auto-enable from sunset to sunrise.
  • Adjust Screen Brightness: When the environment is dark, the screen should be dim too. Many people keep their screen too bright in the dark — this is the most damaging behavior for your eyes. Enable "Auto-Brightness" and make sure it works properly.
  • Maintain Distance: Keep the phone at least 30 cm from your eyes. Many people hold their phones very close, which keeps the ciliary muscle in a state of tension, accelerating nearsightedness.

V. Neck Rescue Guide for "Phone Benders"

When looking down at your phone, your neck bears 5-6 times the pressure of normal standing. Long-term neck bending can straighten the cervical curve, cause bone spurs, dizziness, and hand numbness. Here are some simple improvement methods:

  • Raise Your Phone: When looking at your phone, try to hold it at eye level rather than looking down at your lap. Your arms may get tired, but your neck will thank you.
  • Move Your Neck Every 30 Minutes: Slowly turn your head left to the limit, hold for 3 seconds, return to center; then turn right, hold for 3 seconds. Repeat 5 times. Then do the "rice character exercise" — trace the character "米" (rice) in the air with your chin.
  • Wall Standing for 3 Minutes: Press the back of your head, shoulder blades, buttocks, and heels against a wall. Stand for 3 minutes daily to effectively correct the hunched, head-down posture.

VI. Sleep and Phone — The Bedroom Habit Most Worth Changing

Blue light from your phone screen suppresses melatonin production, making you "more awake the more you look." Many people feel "I'll get sleepy as I scroll," but they're actually being tricked by blue light — when they finally put the phone down, they can't fall asleep. Here are improvement suggestions:

  • No Phone for 1 Hour Before Bed: This is the most effective yet hardest to follow. If you can't manage it, at least turn on "Night Shift/Eye Protection Mode" to minimize blue light.
  • Put the Phone Out of Reach: Put the charger at the other end of the bedroom, not on the nightstand. This way you won't be tempted to pick it up and scroll, and when the alarm goes off, you have to get up to turn it off — killing two birds with one stone.
  • Enable "Sleep Mode": iPhone's "Sleep" Focus can automatically lock the screen and simplify the lock screen during sleep hours; Android brands have similar features.
  • Use an Alarm Clock Instead of Your Phone: Buy a cheap physical alarm clock for a dozen or so yuan. Stop using your phone as an alarm, and you'll escape the trap of "just checking the time, then can't help scrolling."

VII. Information Anxiety — Learn "Selective Blindness"

The amount of information we receive daily equals what people in ancient times received in a lifetime. But the human brain wasn't designed to process this much information — overload leads to anxiety, scattered attention, and decision fatigue. The solution isn't "getting more information" but "actively filtering":

  • Unfollow: Open your list of followed accounts, bloggers, and creators, and ask yourself one question: "Did I get any real value from this in the past month?" If not, unfollow. Quality over quantity for information sources.
  • Turn Off Non-Essential App Notifications: Turn off notifications for all apps except WeChat, phone, SMS, and calendar. News doesn't need push notifications — you'll see it when you actively look.
  • Set an "Information Fast Day": Pick one day a week (e.g., Sunday) to completely avoid phone news and short videos. You'll find the sky doesn't fall, and you'll feel noticeably better on Monday.

Hands-On: One-Week Digital Health Challenge

  1. Today: Open Screen Time / Digital Wellbeing and review last week's usage data.
  2. Tomorrow: Set daily limits for your most time-consuming entertainment apps (recommend 30-60 minutes).
  3. Day after: Schedule Do Not Disturb (22:00-07:00), allowing calls from favorites.
  4. Day 4: No phone for 1 hour before bed; move charger to the other end of the bedroom.
  5. Day 5: Unfollow 5 accounts or bloggers you no longer watch.
  6. Day 6: Try a full day of "information fast" — no news, no short videos.
  7. Day 7: Review this week's Screen Time report and compare with last week.

Chapter Summary

  • First check your screen time data — understanding the current state is the first step to change
  • Set limits for entertainment apps, schedule Do Not Disturb — regain control of your attention
  • The 20-20-20 rule is the simplest and most effective eye care habit
  • Looking down at your phone puts 5-6x pressure on your neck — raise your phone and stretch regularly
  • No phone 1 hour before bed, charger out of reach
  • The antidote to information anxiety is "active filtering," not "getting more"

Chapter 30: Screen Mirroring, Presentations, and Car Connectivity

Your phone screen is at most 7 inches, but your TV is 55 inches and your projector is 100 inches. Casting your phone screen to a larger display is a completely different experience. This chapter covers three high-frequency scenarios: screen casting, presentations, and car connectivity — helping you extend your phone's capabilities to bigger screens.

I. Three Wireless Casting Camps — Don't Mix Them Up

Wireless casting all looks like "phone screen to TV," but there are three underlying technologies that are mutually incompatible:

Technology Who Uses It Protocol
AirPlayiPhone/iPad/MacApple ecosystem, smoothest experience. Requires Apple TV or AirPlay-enabled TV
MiracastAndroid phonesWi-Fi Direct connection, no router needed. Android phones' "wireless casting" uses this by default
DLNAAll platformsOnly pushes media files (video/music/photos), doesn't mirror screen. Good for pushing video to TV for playback
Operation methods for each platform:
  • 3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things Separately: Control Center > Screen Mirroring > Select your TV/Apple TV. If the TV doesn't support AirPlay, you can buy an Apple TV box or an AirPlay-enabled TV stick.
  • iOS: Swipe down the notification panel > Find "Wireless Cast" / "Smart Cast" / "Multi-Screen Interaction" button > Select TV. Phone and TV must be on the same Wi-Fi.
  • Universal Solution: If the TV is too old to support any wireless casting, plug a Chromecast or Xiaomi Box / Huawei Box into the TV's HDMI port to receive casts.

II. Wired Casting — More Stable, Zero Latency

Wireless casting is convenient but has latency, making gaming and presentations unpleasant. Wired casting solves this:

  • 3. Categorized Backup Strategy: Store Important Things Separately: Requires a Lightning/USB-C to HDMI adapter cable (about 100-200 yuan). Plug in, and the phone screen outputs directly to the TV/projector's HDMI port.
  • iOS: Some phones support USB-C to HDMI direct connection (requires DP Alt Mode support; most flagships support it). Just buy a USB-C to HDMI cable.
  • Meeting Room Scenario: If you frequently use your phone for presentations, keep an HDMI adapter cable in your bag. Meeting room TVs/projectors almost all have HDMI ports — just plug in and go, far more reliable than fiddling with wireless casting.

III. Phone Becomes Computer — Desktop Mode

Some Android phones support "Desktop Mode" — when connected to a monitor, the phone outputs a computer-like desktop interface that can be operated with mouse and keyboard:

  • Samsung DeX: Samsung flagship's signature feature. Connecting a monitor brings up a desktop interface with multi-window support, the closest experience to a real computer. With Bluetooth keyboard and mouse, you can travel without a laptop.
  • Huawei Desktop Mode: Huawei Mate series / Pura series also has similar functionality when connected to a monitor. Supports multi-window, file management, and office apps.
  • Motorola Ready For: Moto flagships also support it, with features similar to DeX.
  • What is RAW: Light office work (email, document editing), PPT presentations, watching videos on big screen. Not suitable for heavy Excel work or professional design.

IV. Car Connectivity — The Right Way to Use Your Phone While Driving

Operating your phone while driving is illegal, but navigation, music, and calls are essential. Car connectivity systems let you use your phone's core features on the car's infotainment screen, so the phone can be set aside:

  • Apple CarPlay: Top choice for iPhone users. Connect to the car system via USB or wirelessly, and the car screen shows a streamlined iPhone interface — navigation (Amap/Baidu Maps), music, phone, messages, podcasts. Siri voice control is entirely hands-free.
  • Android Auto: Android users' counterpart. Features similar to CarPlay, supporting Google Maps, Spotify, etc. Some features are unavailable in China due to Google service restrictions.
  • Huawei HiCar: Huawei's proprietary solution, widely supported by domestic car models. Beyond navigation and music, it also supports Huawei video calls, parking camera fusion, and other unique features.
  • Baidu CarLife: Cross-platform solution, works with both iOS and Android. Fewer features but broad compatibility — many older car models only support CarLife.

Private repositories aren't absolutely secure either; sensitive information is best managed with environment variables, not in code repositories.

Regardless of which car connectivity solution you use, always rely on voice control while driving. Set your navigation destination and music playlist before starting to drive — never operate the car screen while in motion.

V. Meeting Room Casting in Practice — No More Panic

Meetings are the most frequent casting scenario and also the most prone to problems. Here are practical tips:

  • Arrive Early to Test: Never wait until the meeting starts to connect casting. Arrive 10 minutes early and test your connection method. Wi-Fi casting fails more often than you'd think.
  • Prepare a Wired Plan B: Keep an HDMI adapter cable in your bag. When wireless casting won't connect, a wired connection is your lifesaver.
  • Disable Notification Preview: When casting, your WeChat messages appear on the meeting room big screen. Before casting, turn off "Lock Screen Notification Content Preview" in settings, or enable "Presentation Mode" (some phones support this — automatically hides notifications during casting).
  • "Present Documents" Rather Than "Operate Your Phone": If you're presenting a PPT, store the file on your phone and open it in WPS for fullscreen playback, rather than casting your entire phone screen. This is more professional and smoother.

Hands-On: Complete a Phone-to-TV Cast

  1. Chapter 18: Data Backup and Migration
  2. Open a photo or video on your phone.
  3. Try wireless casting (iPhone uses Screen Mirroring, Android uses the wireless cast button).
  4. If it fails, check whether the TV supports the corresponding protocol, or try DLNA push (tap the "Cast" button in the Gallery/Video app).
  5. After successful casting, try doing other operations on your phone to see if the big screen mirrors them.

Chapter Summary

  • Three wireless casting camps: AirPlay (Apple), Miracast (Android), DLNA (cross-platform media push)
  • Wired casting is more stable with zero latency — an HDMI adapter cable is essential for meeting rooms
  • Samsung DeX / Huawei Desktop Mode turns your phone into a light office computer
  • Car connectivity: Four major solutions — CarPlay / Android Auto / HiCar / CarLife
  • Meeting room casting golden rules: test early, prepare a Plan B, disable notification preview

Chapter 31: Getting Started with Short Video Shooting and Content Creation

In 2026, short videos are no longer "toys for young people" — they've become the fundamental way everyone gets information and expresses themselves. Whether you want to document your life, share knowledge, or start a side business, your phone is your best creative tool — no need to buy a camera or learn Premiere. A single phone is enough to get started. This chapter helps you start from scratch.

I. Think Before You Shoot: Who's Your Audience?

The first mistake many people make is "picking up the phone and shooting immediately" without knowing who the audience is. Before you start, answer three questions:

  1. Who is my audience?— Content for kids, peers, or elderly viewers requires completely different styles.
  2. What value can I provide?— Make people laugh (entertainment), learn (knowledge), crave (food), or feel warm (emotion). You need at least one.
  3. Which platform can I consistently post on?— Douyin/Kuaishou (general entertainment), Xiaohongshu (lifestyle), Bilibili (in-depth content), WeChat Channels (social circle). Choose one main platform to focus on — don't distribute across all platforms from the start.

II. Phone Camera Basic Settings — 5 Things to Do Before Shooting

  1. Set Resolution to 1080P, Frame Rate to 30fps: This is the standard for short video platforms. 4K files are too large and upload slowly. 60fps has no advantage on social platforms and just creates bigger files.
  2. Clean the Lens: The first and most important tip. Wipe the lens with your clothes before shooting — the image immediately becomes noticeably clearer.
  3. Lock Focus and Exposure: Long-press the subject in the viewfinder for 2 seconds until "AE/AF Lock" appears. This prevents brightness fluctuations while moving during the shot.
  4. Horizontal or Vertical?— For Douyin/Kuaishou/WeChat Channels/Xiaohongshushoot vertically (9:16). For Bilibili/YouTubeshoot horizontally (16:9). Decide the platform first, then the orientation.
  5. Enable Grid Lines: Settings > Camera > Grid. The foundation of rule-of-thirds composition, helping you quickly find the visual center.

III. Five Camera Movement Techniques — Make Your Footage Come Alive

The biggest problem for beginner videographers is footage that's too "static" — standing still the entire time. Learn these five basic camera movements, and your footage will instantly feel more professional:

  • Push: The phone slowly moves toward the subject. Creates tension or intimacy of "approaching."
  • Pull: The phone slowly moves away from the subject. Pulls from detail to wide shot, establishing the environment.
  • Pan: The phone stays in place, rotating left or right. Good for landscapes and showing space.
  • Track: The phone moves parallel, following the subject. Requires steady hands, best with a smartphone gimbal.
  • Follow: The phone follows behind or in front of the subject. The most commonly used movement in vlogs.

Stability Is the Top Priority: Shaky footage looks very unprofessional. Two-handed grip is more stable than one-handed; when walking, bend your knees slightly and use a "ninja walk" to reduce up-and-down bouncing; if you have budget, buy a smartphone gimbal (DJI OM series about 500-800 yuan) — it's a game-changer.

IV. Editing Basics — CapCut Is Enough

JianYing (the domestic version of CapCut) is currently the most beginner-friendly mobile editing tool — free, feature-rich, and template-heavy. Here's the basic workflow:

  1. Import Footage: Open CapCut > New Project > Select and import your video clips.
  2. Trim: Drag the timeline to trim the wasted footage at the beginning and end of each clip. Principle: keep only the parts with information — shorter is better than longer.
  3. Add Transitions: Tap the "Transition" button between two clips and choose a simple transition effect. Beginners should use "Dissolve" or "Fade to Black" — avoid flashy 3D transitions.
  4. Add Subtitles: CapCut has an "Auto Captions" feature that generates subtitles with one tap. Accuracy is about 90% — just manually proofread once.
  5. Add Music: CapCut's music library has many royalty-free tracks. Choose a BGM that matches the rhythm and content, and set the volume to about 1/3 of the original video audio.
  6. Export: Export at 1080P, 30fps, bitrate set to "Recommended."

V. The Importance of Thumbnails — 70% of People Decide Whether to Watch Based on the Cover

A short video's thumbnail is its "storefront" — it determines whether people click. Key points for making thumbnails:

  • Thumbnail Should Have One Sentence: Write the core content of the video in large text, e.g., "Learn Phone Photo Editing in 3 Minutes." Font should be large, colors bright, with contrast against the background.
  • Thumbnail Must Match Content: Don't be a "clickbaiter" — if the thumbnail says one thing but the video shows another, viewers will swipe away immediately, and the algorithm will penalize you.
  • Facial Expressions Should Be Vivid: If the thumbnail has a person, pick a moment with a vivid or exaggerated expression. Human faces attract more clicks than text.
  • Making Thumbnails in CapCut: In CapCut, select the best frame, add text overlay, and export as an image for the thumbnail.

VI. Three Content Creation Principles

  • First 3 Seconds Determine Life or Death: On short video platforms, viewers decide within 3 seconds whether to swipe or keep watching. The first 3 seconds must have a "hook" — a question, a suspense, or a surprising visual.
  • One Video, One Topic: The most common mistake beginners make is cramming too much into one video. One video should solve one problem — thoroughness beats comprehensiveness.
  • Persistence Beats Talent: Algorithmic recommendation requires "warming up the account." The first 20 videos will get almost no views — this is normal. Keep updating 2-3 per week, let the algorithm learn your content direction, and traffic will gradually grow.

Hands-On: Shoot a 30-Second Short Video

  1. Pick a small topic you know well (e.g., "How to make phone fonts larger").
  2. Shoot 3-5 vertical clips, each 5-10 seconds.
  3. Use CapCut to splice, trim, add subtitles, and add BGM.
  4. Create a thumbnail with large text.
  5. Export and send to a friend first for feedback before publishing.

Chapter Summary

  • Think before shooting: who's the audience, what value you provide, which platform to post on
  • 5 things before shooting: 1080P/30fps, clean lens, lock focus/exposure, decide orientation, enable grid
  • Five camera movements: Push, Pull, Pan, Track, Follow — stability is priority #1
  • Edit with CapCut: trim → transitions → subtitles → BGM → export — six steps
  • First 3 seconds are make-or-break, one video one topic, persistence beats talent

Chapter 32: Smartphone Security First Aid Manual

This chapter is an "emergency plan." I hope you never need it, but if your phone is lost, stolen, or you're scammed, this guide will help minimize your losses. I recommend reading through it now, then screenshotting the key steps or printing them out at home — because when something happens, your phone might not be in your hands.

Scenario 1: Phone Lost/Stolen — The Golden 30 Minutes

The first 30 minutes after losing your phone are "golden time" — proper handling can protect your money and privacy. Follow these steps in order, don't skip any:

Standard Operating Procedure for the First 30 Minutes After Loss

  1. Borrow Someone's Phone to Call Your Number（Minute 1): It might just be nearby — a kind person might answer and return it.
  2. Remotely Lock Your Phone（Minutes 2-5): Use someone else's phone or computer to log into the Find service:
    • iPhone: iCloud.com > Find My > Select your device > Mark as Lost
    • Android brands: Huawei cloud.huawei.com / Xiaomi i.mi.com / OPPO cloud.oppo.com etc.
  3. Report SIM Card Lost（Minutes 5-10): Call your carrier's customer service (China Mobile 10086 / China Unicom 10010 / China Telecom 10000), report the phone lost and request SIM card suspension. This step is critical — scammers who get your SIM card can receive verification codes and reset all your passwords.
  4. Freeze Payment Accounts(Minutes 10-20):
    • Alipay: Call 95188 to report loss, or log into Alipay on someone else's phone > Me > Settings > Security Center > Emergency Freeze
    • WeChat: Call 110 to report to police, then contact WeChat customer service, or go to WeChat Security Center > Freeze Account
    • Bank apps: Call the customer service number on the back of your bank card and request online banking freeze
  5. Set a SIM card PIN（Minutes 20-25): Post on your social media or ask family to help spread the word that your phone is lost, preventing scammers from using your identity to trick others.
